Thank you for asking these questions. Really important ✨🙏🏽❤ Answering the questions again @xylia_grey 

1. No, I understand the struggle and journey, even for myself I dabbled in so many things because accessing Korean spirituality was hard. I will say that for me, dabbling in so many things messed me up more. By the time I met my spirit mother, I was all sorts of fucked. But I understand, and hope that can help with accessing Korean spirituality, shamanism and folk magic. Pushing out a few things for 2022 to do just that, speaking and teaching more about folk magic, spirituality and shamanism musok/mugyo. 

2. Girl, my story is long. I was scared, I lived most of my life scared and afraid. Despite my fear, I knew I had to something. It took alot for me voice and fight for what I needed (against my family). I was on the edge of a cliff ready give up on myself and life. It was my son Mason who gave me the courage. I saw similar signs and symptoms in  him. That gave me the push because I wanted to protect him from what I went through. Also the year I got initiated was during Korea President Park removal, a time when ppl hated shamans and mudangs because of that scandal. We had to be discreet when we were traveling for prayers and ceremony just in case to be safe. 

3. This question means so much to me because its the first time in my life I stepped into myself. I have negative relationships with any attention due to bullying and abuse. The thought of being public or showing my face paralyzed me. But my spirits were patience and nudged me. It wasn't until the pandemic and very recent on my social media that I really learned to step into myself unapologetically - flying my freak flag high and proud. (Thank U @chaweonkoo)
It was my grandmother (spirit) who guided me, gave me the courage to transform. 

4. You don't need to be a mudang or a shaman to access healing or transformation. It can be achieved by anyone. The tools we use to aid in that process and transformation may be different but it take self love and courage. Because you are enough and fully capable.

posts.caption:
We are the only fully established and oldest lineage in the US. There is no dispute. 

My spirit mother has worked for the Korean community for the past 25 years plus in America. We perform over 40+ ceremony and rituals EVERY year. From initiations, money, health, sickness, guiding of spirit and souls to traditional rituals. 

Its important to develop relationships with the land and earth consistently - we are always in mountain prayers at Bear Mountain in NY.  Being a mudang in our traditions is maintaining an active role with your spirits.
We actively maintain connection to the earth and land of Korea (our roots) bridging the gods and deities together through our songs. We go on our yearly pilgrimage, renewing our initiations in Korea.

Its been a long and hard journey. Trying to bend with traditions and modern times. 
I am proud of what my spirit mother achieved - as an immigrant speaking no English. And now she is the only fully established lineage and providing the community with access to full 굿 kut/gut ceremony and ritual services. 

Korean shamanism is often described as a surviving tradition....but its strength is in its ability to adapt. It fucking thrives.

posts.caption:
"I was working with another mudang and she instructed me to set up an ancestral altar, make daily offerings of water and liquor. She sent sacred paper written josang 조상 as a placeholder on the altar". 

Please DO NOT do this or listen to this advice ever. The mudang gave improper advice, and has caused more harm to the person. 

People have different ways of expressing their spiritual practices. 
But that was dangerous and misinformed advice. Its dangerous when it backfires and you are now thrown into the winds from the ancestors. Its important that whoever you are working with is properly trained. 
Properly trained meaning -  do they have a teacher, a lineage, a house, ACTIVE with their spirit family in rituals and ceremonies. Ask Questions!!! 
Do they have their own rituals of renewing initiation. If the mudang does not, be a little careful. 

That sacred paper is just mass produced hanji or cheap ritual paper sold at spiritual stores. Using words like that is misleading, making it seem more than it is. There is nothing sacred about writing 조상 on a piece of paper - dont fall for that BS. 

Not my normal content. 
I dont like to engage in things like calling people out. But this is something very important and can cause more harm than good. 

Why is the advice harmful? 
Setting up altars like that invite more spirits and energy. Low energy and homeless spirits Japgwi 잡귀 and Japgwishin 잡귀신. For those who are spiritually and energy sensitive, wrecking havoc around you. Breaking things around you. 

Ancestors must be named! 
Writing Josang 조상 (Ancestors) does nothing and invites ghost in. 
If you don't know your ancestors name, call in the root name (last name). Let's say your grandmother from your dad side (Choi) then write in Choi-ssi Halmoni (Grandmother). And the same for your maternal using their maiden name.

Our practices are real. 
Our spirits are real.
The friends I've lost because of backfire due to improper mudangs are real. 

Spreading misinformation is harmful. 
If you have questions and need verify things, ASK!

Our ancestral and spiritual practice is demonized because its used to empower the people - including us. 

In the words of Kuukuwa Andam: "You are convinced that they are evil & anyone who worships them is wicked. These are the same deities who helped your ancestors live long enough to birth you. Deities who inspired you to keep your environment clean, taught you to have certain rest days from farming & fishing so the land was sustained. Deities you were terrified of lying to & so swearing before them was more effective than any oath created in a foreign land.⁣

posts.caption:
Korean rice cakes and its symbolic connection with the gods and spirits. 

Rice cakes are a traditional foods and used in ceremony. Each rice cake can hold symbolic meanings that's tied to the spirits. 

1. 무지개떡 (Rainbow rice cake)  represents 동자 (boy child) & 동녀 (girl child) the child spirits. 

2. 백설기 (white rice cake) symbolic for 불사 (bulsa) the ancestral guardian deity

3. 팥 시루떡 (Red Bean rice cake) this can be used to represent 대감 (Daegam) god of wealth, prosperity and commerce. 

4. 가래떡 (long cylinder rice cakes) these can be symbolic for 칠성 (Chilseong) god of longevity and life.

These are some of the shamanic meanings behind rice cakes - a traditional offering. For some it's very hard to find and rice cake can be substituted with baked goods and pastries.

I dont how to say this, I struggle with my words. But I'm just gonna say it. 

If anyone is ever to do a 굿 gut/kut ceremony, especially if it's a 내림굿/신굿 (initiation), or a 병굿 (sickness healing), or any 굿. One of the most critical component of the ceremony is the ancestors. 

I know so many who've had initiations and ceremony, where the ancestral gori (part) was skipped over, or not properly done. 
This part of the ceremony requires full possession with all the ancestors from the paternal and maternal. Clothing must be given as an offering to each of the ancestors. They must perform the ritual act of cord cutting, exorcism along with proper storytelling to release their grievances (han). 

With initiation, I understand we are living in modern times but you cannot adjust the ceremony from 3 days to one day, or hours. 
Single day initiation are not legitimate, and its can bring more harm to you - viewed as disrespecting the spirits. I've lost friends because ceremony was improper. 

Please use caution. 
Its so important. 
Succession of the ceremony  depends on the ancestor gori segment of the ceremony. 
Let me know if you have questions.

posts.caption:
만니산 - Mani Mountain. 

At the summit peak of this mountaintop sits a stone altar  built by Danggun (god king of Korea) himself. 

A sacred site where Heaven can touch earth. There two sacred altars in Korea,  used to make offerings and sacrifice to the Heavens. One altar is located in Mani mountain, the other located at the summit of Taebaek mountain. 

Took this video on my pilgrimage at the summit. The altar was closed to the public at time of visit. 

It was a bit sad that the sacred mountain was gated up. The local shopkeeper said it was to prevent "those people" from entering. 
She meant mudangs. 
Then the shock and embarrassment when she realized that we were. 
The buddhist temples put entrances and gates to sacred mountains, essentially owning it. The mountains do not belong to temples or organizations, they belong to the people.

Mom's hands are medicine hands. 

My baby woke up (4am) with a sore throat, he panicked and started to cry. He was nervous and anxious thinking he had covid. There's been a few cases in his school already. We took him for a Covid test and luckily its negative. 

I brewed him a cup of warm 보리차 barley tea to soothe and calm. Brought down our blankets and watching Magic School Bus cartoons in the living room. He's happy and its all that matters.

엄마 손이 약손.
엄마 손이 약손.
Mama hands are medicine hands. 
Mama hands are medicine hands. 

Looking back this is the first form of folk magic I learned. 
It's something I continue with my children passing this down. The hands of our mothers and matriarch holds healing and wisdom.

posts.caption:
Name changing. 

I didnt understood the importance of names when I was younger. I grew up with multiple name changes throughout my life.

At birth, I was named MinJung (민정). After the my parents divorce, my father changed my name and not my siblings - weird. 
Back then, calling Korea was expensive and phone conversations were short. Through heavy static phone connection, my grandmother prescribed me a new name and identity. My new name is HyeonJung (형정). 

It took a while for the new name to settle in, I didn't like it - but did what I was told by the family elders. 
Grandma flew in to live with us, a year or so later. Turns out the name my grandmother gave is yoonjung (윤정), my dad heard it wrong. So my identity and name changed again. 

When I was baptized I was named Maria, and my dad made motions to change it permanently but later fell through. 

After my initiation, I was given the name 장군보살 (Janggun Bosal) but had to change it again. Spirit mom gave me a new name 신수보살 (Sinsu Bosal). And now, everyone just calls me Mudang Jenn. 

Pictured laying on a rock, with flower patterned pants. Legs crossed looking out to the river. 

#koreanshaman #mudang #mugyo #musok #koreanspirituality #koreanamerican #koreandiaspora #asianamerican

The 5 elements in Korean astrology represents different planets. 

Wood represents Jupiter.
Fire represents Mars.

Saju Series 1/3: 사조 Saju Korean Astrology known as the 4 pillars of destiny - a branch of Chinese astrology using the 5 element philosophy.

A birth natal chart consists of 4 pillars, each one have its own meaning and symbolism. 
We identify based on our birth year zodiac - but that's misleading when reading saju. The zodiac sign you were born in has little to do with your personality or characteristics. 

✨ The year pillar represents your surroundings, social environments, relationships with friends, family, colleagues. You can also find your ancestors energy in this pillar, and your early childhood. 

✨ The month pillar represents your work and career. The type of worker you are and your skills. Your parents information and energy is in this pillar. 

✨ The day pillar contains the most important element in the chart - your daymaster. Your true element. Your character and personality, how your grow and deal with things. This pillar also contain the energy of your romantic relationships, love and commitments.

✨ The year pillar represents your future goals, dreams and aspirations. Its also the children pillar. If you are a business owner or employer, represents the relationships with employees and staff.

The year you were born, your zodiac sign (띠) just means that Jupiter was in that placement at time of your birth. The 12 zodiacs represents the 12 postions that Jupiter phased through.

If you are born year of Tiger 🐯 범띠, it means that's where Jupiter was positioned.

posts.caption:
Let's talk about money 💸💰. 
In the Korean shamanic tradition the god to oversee wealth, money and business commerce is 대감 (Daegam) or 여대감 (Yeo-Daegam) the female version. Money holds energy, value and intentions - its called currency for those reasons. 

During a 굿 gut/kut ceremony, whole pigs or the pighead is given as an offering. Money is dipped in makgeoli (Korean rice wine) and put into the mouth, nose, ears, etc. 

Money is used as offerings given to the dead and ancestors. 노잣돈 (Noja-don) is  given to the spirits so that they can pay for expenses in the afterworld. 

Money is folded and tied into the fabric called 고 (go) during ceremony. As the knots unravel with the money tied, it's given as offerings to the guardians or gate keepers of the underworld. Money is also used to appease 한 (Korean han) and grievances. 

Paper talisman lanterns with coin cutouts are used to help "light the way" for spirit as they travel to the afterworld, spirit world. These money offerings and paper coins can be used to pay the ferryman or ferry guide to help the spirit cross over. 

But let's not ignore the destructions of capitalism even in our shamanic traditions. Its a huge issue of over-consumption,  mass productions with lots of waste. Its influences can attribute alot of harm, putting families into debt, possibilities of getting scammed or worse. 

Although I am traditionally trained for over 5 years, but the way I want to practice is different - breaking walls of social issues within our traditions. 
Like a baby bird 🐦preparing to fly out of the nest - ready to take a leap of faith, spread my wings and letting the winds of my spirits and ancestors to carry me. 

• • • • • • • •
Pictured is ceremonial cloths of white, yellow and black knotted with 20 USD folded in.

Back home again from the mountains and rivers. I find water to be incredibly healing, grounding and restorative. 

🏞Water is incredibly sacred, respected and worshipped. 

People will climb mountains to drink from its spring waters believing in its medicinal and energy qualities. Our ancestors knew to protect waters and rivers to receive the blessings and guidance of spirits. 

Our ancestors bathe in the rivers not for hygiene but for spiritual protection, purification and to renew energy. 

Fresh water given as offerings to the gods and spirits is called 옥수 물 (oksu-mul) means jade water. Washing away the unclean - purification symbolism and process. 

Water is also the bridge, the gateway which helps separates our physical humanly world with the spiritual. 
The journey of a spirit will board a boat with a ferryguide , paying their token fees to cross over to the afterworld. 

Water is the most simplest offering. The folkmagic ritual 비손 bi-son only requires water offering and your prayers. 

How important is water in your spiritual practice?

posts.caption:
This upcoming Saturday (8/14) is Chilseok day. 

Its an important time for farmers. Marks the coming of the wet season, a symbol for abundance. 
My grandmother was a rice farmer and merchant, they worked closely with the land performing rituals for abundance and blessings. 

Grandmother would set a small offering table of fruits, and rice cakes, along with candle, incense, freshly poured water and liquor. 

She would make wheat pancakes of simply just flour and water. Similar to a crepe,  used red beans to write chilseok - set as offerings. 

Water is left out overnight to collect the energies of the big dipper (chilseong - God of longevity) to use in folk magic. 

Pictured are purple blooms of bellflower, roots are used as sacred medicine.

posts.caption:
Aug 14th on the Lunar calendar is 7/7, its 칠석 Chilseok Day - to celebrate Chilseong 

Most associated this day with the mythology of two lovers separated by the Milky Way galaxy - a celebration of the lovers reunion. 

Shamanically, Its a very important day for those with young children in the family. its a day to pay respect and devotional ritual and offerings for Chilseong. 

Chilseong is the god of life, and longevity. Rituals performed on this day is dedicated to Chilseong to pray for the health and longevity of  children. 

Children information is written on a long white (color to represent purity and cleaniness) fabric that symbolizes their lifeline. Set on the altar along with offerings, this devotional ritual protects children. 

In next post, I will also share the folk magic ritual that's been performed in my family by the matriarch, and how its performed shamanically.

posts.caption:
Our indigenous ways are rooted in our gods. Christians express their faith carrying the Bible and crosses for their God. 

But our gods is the sun, the wind, the rivers, oceans, the stars and moon,  the tree that grows and flowers that bloom. Birds chirp and brings messages from spirits, butterflies bring love and luck. Being in nature, taking a moment to appreciate earth beauty is being connected to the gods - in the simplest form. 

Even as a mudang, when our energies are low and our spirits calls us - we retreat to the mountains or the oceans, to be held in their embrace and bosom. We spend time with the earth in laughter and in gratitude. 

This picture is taken in 토성명 Toseongmyung in 강원도 Gangwon-do in 2017. Woke up early morning to watch the sun rise as I had a heart to heart with my soul and spirits. 

Been thinking about creating a trip with a small group to go back to Korea and doing a shamanic tour. Visiting sacred sites, mountains and oceans to pay respects to our ancestors, gods and spirits. Working on it.

Taken last year. 
Looking back at the year, I've had some major break throughs, transformations and awakenings. The older version of myself would be proud, and thinking about brings tears. 

I've learned to step out of the shadow, and really work on my self - growing. I realize now, the only person that was stopping myself from growth was me. I allowed many years of trauma and abuse to hold its power over me and to sway me. 

Working on yourself isn't shameful. Undoing whats been handed to you by family is part of breaking familial and ancestry pain and trauma. I've died many deaths, literally and figuratively. 

The biggest thing holding me back was - what others thought of me, especially my father since he doesnt know who I am - a Korean mudang. I felt the weight of my family's narrow judgement preventing my growth. And quite honestly its exhausting and I dont really give a fuck what their discrimimatory views and opinions are. 

This time it feels different, I walk with more power in my steps. I'm going to be sharing alot more about my past, my path and future goals.

Totally unapologetic, and if there's a problem - I'm sorry, you're just gonna have to deal with it. 
Rawr. 🦁

When we go for mountain prayers & ritual.
Two altars are set, the main altar for the gods and another for 서낭당 (Seonandang) a dedicated tree guardian. It's believe during the Mongolian invasion, the power of our seonang (tree guardians) that helped defeat.

서난당 Seonangdang, the shrine's are described as a village tree guardians, and protectors of passing travelers but the roles and involvement is much more.

Its also a sacred place where we can release suffering spirits and ancestors. Or we can bind malicious spirits and ancestors. A space where the guardians can make spirits work on polishing their rock, a place of in between and transitioning. A sacred space of cleansing, purification and exorcism. 

According to wiki, the most famous 서난 is the town of Jeonju. Woot woot, shout out to my Jeonju Yi lineage clan!

Picture is the tree guardian shrine at Sun Moon Mountain in Korea. Took on my previous pilgrimage and prayer to Korea.

posts.caption:
Korea had many names and titles, through history. "The land of the morning calm" is an English nickname created and popularized by Percival Lowell in 1885.

Korea had many names...but once was known as "the land of leopards". 
Leopards roamed the Korean peninsula, even outnumbered the tigers. Leopards were feared and source of many folk stories. Even in folk paintings and art, leopards are drawn comically and paired with magpies. Leopards were hunted to extinction during the Occupation and were even referred as the Korean leopard. 

Pictured is my 산신 신복 (Sanshin sinbok) ceremonial spirit regalia of the Mountain god with Leopard motifs.

posts.caption:
9 years ago this June, I was fired from the Sapphire NYC strip club, working as a supervisor/manager. During that time I was  a heavy cocaine user - spending more or less $400 a night, almost overdosing twice. 

I walked out of a 6 year abusive relationship, packed my bag with no where to go. I ended up homeless and eventually lived off a friend's couch. It was truly a difficult time with no one to rely on. 

Despite the hardships, and lack of stability I was incredibly clear minded. This very moment of my life is when I had my spiritual awakening. 

With bags packed, and no where to go. I ended up at the playground, and went on the empty swings. The sun was warm, and the breeze gently caressed my face - as I looked up to the sky.

At the exact moment, thinking of spirits and ancestors. The swing right next to me started to swing back and forth, along with me. It felt so warm and comforting like falling into a soft blanket. 

My guardians, ancestors and spirits have always been with me - even at my darkest days and moments. Blood of warriors and healers within me.  They've always been there to uplift me into becoming who I am today. 

And I am totally fucking unapologetic about it. 

I want to take the time and thank my amazing friend ❤ @hichaweon for always supporting me, encouraging me to be more visible and sharing my many, many stories.

posts.caption:
Ceremonial chaos. 
Many parts to a 굿 kut ceremony, its customized and catered to each unique person and/or family. 

Calling the ancestors of your familial lineage and blood. A moment when each ancestor is acknowledged and heard,  sharing their stories and pain. We share tears and laughter with the spirits, a ceremonial union. 

Just like when we go through life difficulties, having support and a safe place is important. A kut ceremony provides a purified (safe) environment, opening the spirits doors giving space to the ancestors express their han, to grieve or share joys. Its a time of healing for us and the spirits.  Ancestral work is important, to work on ancestral pain and trauma that's been past down to us. 

It's what can you do for your ancestors - when we nuture, feed and take care the roots of a plant....the plant is healthy.

posts.caption:
Becoming initiated or a mudang, does not magically erase your karma. I dont know who is spreading false teachings - its very dangerous, harmful and misleading. Please use caution and discernment. 

Being an spiritual open vessel means we have to be constantly aware of the spiritual energies around us. That means that mudangs can be influenced by ghost and low spirits posing as ancestors and deities. 

We must be in continuous ritual and ceremony, to maintain contact and relationship with their gods and spirits. Having an initiation ceremony isn't enough. 

I know firsthand and understand that there is a huge lack of access to information and resources about Korean folk magic and shamanism. Even books written by academia isn't able to fully explain our shamanism.

posts.caption:
Today is "부처님 오는 날, "Day that Buddha arrived" or otherwise known as Buddha's Birthday.

Its a day when people visit temples, sponsor lanterns to hang in the shrine, prayers and blessings, and sharing a meal of various namul in barley rice.

Pictured is the altar and shrine for Buddha's Sarira enshrined on 오대산 Odae Mountain at Woljeongsa 월정사 (head temple) of the Jogye Order. Taken in Fall 2017 during a sacred pilgrimage, every sacred mountain is occupied by a Buddhist temple in Korea. 

Shoutout to my spirit sister Mia, its her birthday- initiation anniversary.

posts.caption:
개나리 (Gae-nari) Golden bells, Forsythia flowers. 
These flowers bloomed overnight, carried my little basket to gather these tender blossoms. The fruit of these flowers are used in traditional medicine for thousands of years. 

These flowers portrays the spring season in Korea. Grandma always taught me that when these flowers bloom - spring is coming.

In the old days, flower crowns were made with these blooms and they were placed by the kings on the head of scholars when successfully passed civil exams, entitling them to an official rank (Flowers and Folklore from Far Korea by Florence Crane)

Yellow color represents the center of the 4 directions, the heavens. But in divination, with the 5 colored flags - yellow color represents our ancestors. 💛 Our ancestors are with us.

posts.caption:
Homage to my Northern roots. 
백김치 White Kimchi. This kimchi is known for being refreshing and cool 시원해. Known as a Northern style kimchi. 

A different variation than the spicy red kimchi. Before the war, and seeking refuge in the South. My family comes from the Northern part of Korea in both my lineages before settling just outside the DMZ. 

When washing machines was first introduced back then, my grandma 👵 actually used it to drain the cabbage from the salt water - putting it on a spin cycle. 🤣🤣. Still working on getting the family recipe. 

I think alot about my roots and where my ancestors come from, and now - we arent allowed back in obviously due to politics and many other issues. I was so grateful to have visited the DMZ border and finally see  금강산 (Diamond Mountain) from a distance. One of the many mountains my grandmother had to climb for her life and freedom - leaving behind her family. Being the sole survivor.  And here I am now, walking in this path to pay homage and respect to all my ancestors before me.

Not my picture, from Google 

 #koreanroots #koreanfood #koreanculture #whitekimchi #kimchi #ancestralguides #ancestors #ancestralhealing #ancestry #koreandiaspora #koreantradition #connectingtonature #matriachs  #grandma #blessing

posts.caption:
Its been 4.5 years since walking this path and I've been able to meet & connect with so many. 

I received an email, asking why my prices was expensive. They explained that they've worked with other mudangs and spirit workers. Then further inquired where my money is being spent. The asker was genuinely asking without trying to be rude and was really nice and kind. I answered the email in the best way I can - explaining what I do, and where I spend my money on. I was incredibly appreciative of the open and kind communication we had compared to the way others approached this with me. This is not to attack or shame the person who emailed but to show how a conversation can take place about this openly. 

Other people asked for healing ceremony and argued that healing should be free, or spirit work is free. You can't pour from an empty cup. When I have to explain my right to make an earning and support my family was incredibly upsetting.

A spirit sister complained (threw a tantrum) that I had a wider reach and following on social media as if that equates to money or something. She worked a normal job, living a single life while I depended on my spiritual work supporting my family with no other means.

My sessions are listed as 1 hour, but its 2 hours - the longest was 6hrs. Other mudang or spirit  workers may have jobs or other work to support themselves - but I dont. 

I dedicate my time/life to train in the traditional healing arts without any means of other financial income. I dont get any tax incentives or special writeoffs. I pay for everything like everyone else. 
It's interesting being in this position, called and accused of many things from others  like clout-chasing 🤣 when I am just sharing my path and stories. 

I've been supported by amazing female creators - that reminded me that I need to keep moving and opening myself to opportunities  instead of putting myself in a corner to continue doing my work as a mudang. I'm so damn grateful for their support and guidance, because in my hard times they kept cheering me on. Just as my gods and spirits have always held me up and provided.

And so thankful to everyone here on IG for the love and support. Always.

⁠

received more than 2,800 self-reports of coronavirus discrimination nationwide, from verbal harassment to physical assault.⁠
⁠
Yet news outlets and federal agencies have been slow to recognize the threat and enact policy changes. For much of the past year, the Justice Department resisted calls from Democratic lawmakers and activists to proactively combat the public targeting of Asians. In the days before Lunar New Year, when surveillance cameras captured a spate of violent, unprovoked attacks against Asian seniors, top-rated cable networks spent little to no airtime covering the issue, according to the progressive research center @MediaMattersforAmerica.⁠
⁠
Amid institutional indifference, social media and other digital tools have allowed Asian Americans to prove the various forms of discrimination they’ve long experienced, organize mutual aid groups and pressure authorities to respond.⁠
⁠
“Social media is an equalizing force not previously available to marginalized communities,” Manjusha Kulkarni, executive director at the Asian Pacific Policy and Planning Council and a co-founder of Stop AAPI Hate, told @NBCAsianAmerica.⁠
⁠
More at @NBCAsianAmerica in their BIO Link.

posts.caption:
Today we are cleaning up both our yards, tidying up. Planning out, mapping out where the raised garden beds will be. 

This year planting some special seeds Korean white dandelions, bottle gourds, joseon pumpkin ❤

I grew with my maternal grandparents (before my parents divorce) and we spent everyday in the community garden. My grandparents along with other immigrant elders turned a local dump into a thriving natural farming community in the 90s - in Flushing.

In the summer I make my rounds around the community garden exchanging our garden goods with the others. I grew up digging in the soil, playing in a field of cosmos under the care of the community elders. 

My grandma and I would push our little cart. And sell vegetables on the street sidewalks of Flushing - right by Union street and Roosevelt. 

I reunited with grandma when I was about 16, she was already in the hospital. Everday I stopped by to massage her, and reposition her to prevent sores on her body. Later she was moved to another facility. She passed away, but my mother didn't tell. It wasn't until a week after her funeral did I learn about her passing. 

I was upset and angry at my mom for robbing that opportunity to say goodbye and pay my respects.  And so I return back to the earth, digging in her soul as an act and tribute to my grandmother. I miss her, but she is with me as my ancestral guide and spirit - guiding me on this path as a spiritworker. 

I share that with my children as we explore the miracles of growing our food and our soul.

posts.caption:
Altar Offerings - FRUITS symbolizes abundance, wealth and fertility.

I often get questions about what types of offerings are allowed in the Korean folk traditions. In older times, offerings mattered depending on the region and what was available locally and choices limited. 

Nowadays with modern technology and logistics, we have access to fruit and food from all over the world than before. 

I was taught that peaches and other stone fruits are avoided. This has to do with peach tree being used for exorcism in chasing away negativity and warding off evil. Stone fruits only have one seed/pit and avoided but fruits with many seeds are used to symbolize abundance. 

Sometimes this is even confusing for me, peaches are avoided for another reason because of the fur fuzz on the skin but yet kiwis 🥝 are okay to use. 
Roses or any plants with thorns are avoided because it deter and prick the spirits but yet pineapples 🍍 are used. 
Fruits with only one pit/seeds are avoided but yet avocados 🥑are acceptable.

But the true power of the talisman is in its effect and protection - it matters who you get your talismans from. Amulets made to protect the homes, used in the welcoming the energy of spring can be drawn by anyone. 

Depending on the purpose, purchasing one sheet of a talisman and amulet effect is minimal. 
For example, drawing a talisman for the harmony and protection of a home requires multiple talisman layered and compounded together. Each having a purpose and specific intentions. 

You don't need to refresh or renew your talisman each year - it truly depends on the TYPE of amulet and its purpose.  Personal talismans are given pouches to carry, and should never be opened as its sealed to contain energy. Once open the seal is broken and the protective energy is released, the talisman become ineffective and useless.

Being a Korean diaspora I was disconnected to the ways of our roots. I am grateful to my ancestral guides for leading me on this path even though its hard as hell. 

I will be posting more in details about the rituals, rites and symbolism in our Korean culture. I find myself falling in love with our traditions every day. 
Thank you for being here.  Really looking forward to learning together ✨

posts.caption:
The Great Full Moon 대보름 Offerings - 약밥.

One of the special dishes prepared is 약밥 yak-bap translate to medicinal rice for its use of honey. Honey is known for its medicinal qualities and referred to as 약 yak medicine in older times. 

약밥 history is recorded in Samguk Yusa, and tied to a story how a crow saved a Silla King when the Queen was plotting his death. 

Rituals and rites in the winter season used 약밥 as offerings in place of fruit when its out of season. 

I pour my heart into making this 약밥 offering, to give my gratitude to the Heavens, spirits and ancestors. 

Food is medicine. 

Pictured brown glutinous rice cake with pumpkin seeds, pine nuts, chestnuts and jujube.

posts.caption:
Great Full Moon 대보름 Offering Preparations. 

This Full moon is known as 대보름 DaeBoreum which means the Great Full Moon. Its the last day of celebration for the Lunar New Year festival.

Specific offerings to prepare for this celebration. 보름 나물 boreum-namul  translates to full moon vegetables which refers to dried vegetables from previous harvest. The dried vegetables are individually prepared. 

오곡밥 Ogok bap known as 5 grain rice is made of glutinous rice mixed with different beans and grains from previous harvest. 

There are mythology stories and various folk beliefs that are  associated with these dish, that I will share later. These offerings are made to the Heavens, spirits and ancestors to petition for bountiful harvest that year. 

There are several festive activities to do to celebrate the Great Full Moon of the Lunar New Year like the burning of the Moon house, charcoal in a tin car, lantern lighting, drinking specialized liquor, selling your 'heat', etc. 

Wishing everyone an amazing Great Full Moon, and Lantern festival. ✨🏮

posts.caption:
House Spirits. 가신 Gasin is important in the Korean culture and folk magic tradition. 
Lunar New Year Offerings for the house spirits.

Homes are sacred and holding energy from the land and within itself. Its proper to pay respect for our sacred home and spaces.

Kitchen spirit, 조왕신 Jowang-shin. Mythology says that Jowangshin (kitchen goddess) is the wife of the roof beam god 성주 Seongju. 

On this day, people put sticky taffy or sticky rice cake by the opening of the hearth in the kitchen. The kitchen spirit is a scribe, a recording everything that happens within the home. The goddess travels to Heaven, to give their report to the gods. 
Putting sticky taffy is believed to block the mouth of the kitchen spirit so they won't be able to tattle on you.

posts.caption:
Hide your shoes!

My grandfather taught me alot about folk traditions through his stories. Night before Lunar New Year, you must hide your shoes - putting it away. A misbehaving spirit will come and bring calamity and ill fortune by trying on your shoes and taking it. 

Baskets and sieves were hung up by the entrys and doorways. A spirit will become distracted and mesmerized by the holes in the basket - enchanted, it be there counting the holes till sunrise. A spirit boobytrap of sorts.

Later on through researching I read that these misbehaving spirits are called 야광귀 ya-gwanggi. (Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture). 
Hair was collected and burned (spirits really dislike the smell of burnt hair.) The ashes are sprinkled by the front and doorway of the home to repel. 

Pictured is colorful children shoes made in the traditional Korean style. These shoes are on my altar for my child spirits, these shoes are just so cute.

posts.caption:
Korean Astrology. 
What is SAJU? 

Rooted from Chinese Bazi astrology.
The astrology uses philosophy of interpreting elemental yin/yang forces. This astrology system is centered and mainly focused on ONE PLANET.
(Take a guess?)

Our ancestors were great scholars of the nights sky, observing the heavens, the stars and the planets. Creating star charts and maps - one the oldest representation of our stars. 

Building the oldest observatory in Asia - the 선덕여왕 Cheomseondae means the star gazing tower. Built in the 7th C during Silla's first reigning female monarch Queen Seondeok. 
*(There is also a drama made about her life, one of my faves). 

Saju is all based on the planetary movement of JUPITER, and the elements corresponds to the position of this planet as it revolves. The elements also represent different planets. 

This system is used in China, Korea, Japan Vietnam and many other Asian countries.

posts.caption:
동지 (Dongji) - Winter Solstice is this Monday (Dec 21). A very particular type of winter solstice, specifically called 애동지 (Ae Dongji). 

On winter solstice, family would gather to make and eat red bean porridge known as 팥죽 (patjuk). But this year, we won't cook and eat the red bean porridge because its an ae-dongji 애동지 - its believed that harm can come to children. Meaning that this winter solstice eating patjuk can leave children unprotected. 

To kinda further explain, one teacher from Korea said that because red bean porridge is used for its exorcism  abilities - Samshin 삼신할매 (goddess of childbirth, and protector of children) CANT come and protect the children during this time if the porridge is consumed or used. 

On winter solstice, I normally prepare a spread of numerous offerings along with bowls of red bean porridge. Each room in the home will also have a bowl placed to cleanse the  home. In older times doors are marked, walls and fences are splattered with the red bean porridge to drive out negative spirits.

Neighbors and villagers would gather in communal exorcism ritual, driving out these negative forces from their homes and village. 

But this year being special, and as a mom with young children I wont be setting up offerings or doing any folk ritual in observance to 애동지.

posts.caption:
A man named 손동지 Son Dongji was exile to Jejudo island, and due to a windstorm his boat crashed. He ended up washed up on the shores of 호동 Hodong village which translates to Tiger Place. 

The villagers was constantly preyed and attacked by the stalking tigers. The villagers decided to flee to the nearby 모도 Modo Island on a raft/boat, unknowingly leaving behind 뽕 할머니 Grandmother Ppong. 

Everyday Ppong Grandmother prayed to the 용왕님 (Yongwang) Dragon King of the Sea in hopes to reunite with her family and villagers. One day Yongwang appeared in her dreams, told her  rainbow 🌈 will fall over the sea, to guide her across to 모도 Modo Island. 
The next day Grandmother Ppong went to the sea, prayed to the Dragon King and  bridge with a rainbow appeared. 

When a bridge with rainbow above appeared, the villagers of Modo grabbed their gongs and percussion - banging on it, to find Grandmother Ppong. They found that she collapsed, and her last words was "나의 기도로 바닷길 열려 너희들을 만났으니 이젠 한이 없다". "Through my prayers, I was able to open the sea road and meet you, I have no more han (deep rooted grievances)" 

Grandmother Ppong ascended to the heavens became a god called 영등 Yeongdeung (god sea and wind). The villagers renamed the village from 호동 Hodong to 회동 Hoedong. 
Every year  annually when the sea bridge appear villagers from both Modo and Hoedong, cross over to meet while they collect seafood, gifts from the sea. 
Its become a sacred place where people pray for fishermans, abundance from the sea and their own wishes. 
This is one of the many stories of Korea's costal island where the myths are still alive and told. Jindo Island historically been used as a refuge during the Mongol invasion, well known for their special dog breeds called Jindo dog (진돗개). 
 
In 1975, a French ambassador Pierre Landy calls Jindo sea parting as the Korean moses miracle referring to the biblical parting of the Red Sea. 
Which makes me 😤AF

posts.caption:
Its time I say this, hopefully to clarify any misinformation. 

I am NOT a tarot card reader or work with any cards - I cannot give you the card of the day, or pull out a card for a quick yes/no. 
I am definitely not a hotline 1800 psychic. I dont give out free readings to advertise my services. This is not to disrespect to any practioners that work in those ways. I know so many respectable practioners who do but it is not my way of working. 

I work in the ways of my Korean ancestry. My divination sessions are different, using tools like coin tossing, rice throwing and flag pulling. Working with these items are directly related to the deities of our folk and indigenous beliefs. Our tradition even casting bones, rocks and sticks to read the energies and divinate.

Once I had a "psychic" come over to hang out, when I mistaken it for a session. She asked for advice and watched me pull flags and work in my ways. She asked why I use my tools as a crutch, when she can just use her clairvoyance without tool's. 
Let me attempt to clarify this.  Working with gods means to work in a mutual partnership, requires a relationship and conversations with the spirits - using those tools is a way to communicate and verify. 

Maybe @tweedandspandex and I should have another IG Live to discuss this.

posts.caption:
Homemade 약밥 is the 💣. 
약밥 yak-bap literally translates to medicine rice. 

When considering the precious ingredients it took to make this rice cake, it really shows that  food is medicinal. 

When fruits were scarce especially in the winter time, 약밥 was used as offering food in rites, rituals and ceremonies. 

We are spoiled by today's convienent instant culture that we have taken for granted a shitload. Rice was so valuable that if it spilled onto the floor, every grain was picked up. 

Had an elderly grandfather client, and he shared his stories with me. When he was a child, he thought that the best time of the year was harvest season. 
Asked him why and he said, because its the only time they get to eat a meal till they were full. 

💔😭

I think of persimmons hanging on trees, rice paddies turned to a golden yellow. 

In older times, especially in a village setting they would have 고사 (gosa) or 게 (je) to mark the first day of autumn. 
The numerous guardian spirits of the village, spirits of the home were all paid tribute in forms of offerings and prayers -by the villagers in communal celebration. 

Our current society may not be like an agriculture based community like those villages. But the importance, the sacredness of our food and agriculture has not diminished. 

• • • • • • • • • • •

I have never taken this long to unpack after a move. This move was extremely difficult for me, but we are starting to settle in. 
Hooooray. 
I plan on making altars all around the outside yard, and erect 장승 totem poles and 솟대 spirit bird poles. 🙏🏽❤

I am thrilled to announce that my new film installation 'Four Months, Four Million Light Years' (2020) is part of the 11th Berlin Biennale, opening today
 
‘Four Months, Four Million Light Years’ (2020) is a shamanic healing journey addressing the colonial narratives behind interracial and intercountry adoption, specifically the historical relations between The Netherlands and Korea. The film takes the colonial print ‘Een Schaman ofte Duyvel-Priester’ (Shaman or Devil’s Priest from the Tungus) (1692) by the Dutchman Nicolaes Witsen as the starting point for a spiritual journey through time. The seventeenth-century print is the first Western depiction of a shaman. It marks the beginning of a long history of racialized and infantilizing descriptions of Asian people by white Europeans. The caricature image was later used by missionaries to marginalize shamanism.

‘Four Months, Four Million Light Years’ time-travels from contemporary Dutch society to the participation of 3,418 Dutch soldiers in the deadly Korean War (1950–1953) to early Dutch colonial descriptions of Asian people. The artist herself is an adoptee from Korea and grew up in The Netherlands. In The Netherlands alone around 40,000 people have been adopted from the Global South to the Global North, often through child trafficking and with falsified documents. The “four months” of the title refer to the time it took to make a Korean child available for the lucrative interracial adoption industry that flourished after the Korean War, an industry that continues to live off the same colonial imagery from 300 years ago. 

In the room, textile banners surround the video projection. Here, shamanic poems, songs and visions invoke the ancestors for support. The work is an homage to those who have been cut off from their mothers, fathers, family, ancestors, land, culture and spirits.

Co-produced by the @kunstenfestivaldesarts

posts.caption:
Today blessings 고사 ritual for a new business to serve the N. Williamsburg, Brooklyn community. 
We set a temporary altar with 5 types of fruit, water, rice wine, soju liquor, specific rice cakes, candy, cookies, rice, 3 types of vegetables, 3 types of fritters and a whole pig. 
The offerings itself takes a long time to prepare and set up. We had shoji paper to burn in the space for purification but noticed the sprinklers above so we abandoned that part. 

This ritual pays respect to the land spirits of this premise, the spirits within the building and the business space. We call in and invoke the gods to this space, especially 지신 and 대감. 

This is our tradition that has been passed down for centuries. Each ritual and ceremony is customized and none is like the other. People often come to us, putting in their faith and its such a big responsibility.
I shadow my spirit mother to learn in the ways of our spirits, our culture and the stories of our ancestors.

posts.caption:
Continued from previous post. 

The neophyte was nervous, and throughout the initiation she kept apologizing for NOT jumping hard enough or high enough. We kept reassuring her that it wasnt the jumping in the initiation that mattered. 
I dont think to this day, she fully understands what we really meant. 

We kept in touch, had many discussions. I always pushed for open communication, always asked for honesty. As time passed, she spoke ill of us, meanwhile smiling in our faces. It was insulting and belittling that she would lie to us, our gods and lineage. She began to stray from our teachings. Doing things without proper training or authorization from our elder. Misuing information, taking advantage of others and abusing sacred trust. 
Soon people started to contact me about her damage and questionable doings. When I decided to confront her, she completely shut down the conversation - not allowing me to speak. 

A few days after the initiation, spirit mom sat me down to have a conversation. She criticized me for picking a fruit off a tree that was not yet riped or matured. How insulting it was to her gods, opening doors of the lineage - and the initiate rejecting this. 

Spirit mom said, this path is not for everyone regardless if they possess gifts from the spirits. Your gifts and talents alone wont carry you far without humility and becoming humble. She again reminded me sternly - you are not a mudang because you are special or above anyone else. You are here to serve your community, the people and our gods - to polish your rock because its shit. 🥺
This is the lesson I share with those who I bring into the lineage, and those selected few that I train. 

Spirit mom urges me to become more vocal about this. She gives full permission to be more public and denounce any claims from training with us - misleading others because we are a closed tradition.

posts.caption:
A story. 

A while ago, before the initiation of a neophyte mudang-to-be. The spirits sent messages through my dream..

We received her 신복 regalias, made and sent from Korea. Spirit mom and I opened the box of her spirit regalia but something was wrong. 
The colors of our spirits regalia, the colors of our shamanism is bright and bold. The colors of her regalia was washed out and dull, I was so shocked to see the spirits regalia looking so tattered and worned. We hung up her spirit clothes, then the box started to purge out black chicks. 
The 신당 shrine of my spirit mother began to fill up with black baby chicks. I woke up unsure of the meaning and message of this dream - one thing I know is they were not good signs -bad omens. 
I ran over to spirit mother to share the details of my dream. I was anxious, scared and nervous. 
Spirit mom was concerned, said 'this child will later stray the wrong path' and the black chicks are those people who will follow her unknowingly. I spent the rest of the day in deep conversation with my elder about options, choices, fate and destinies. 

Initiation day finally arrived, a long 3 day ceremony thats utterly bittersweet. On the second day, the initiate began to have doubts, started to cry telling us she regretted this. She wanted us to stop, pack up her bags to leave and go home. She asked me to take her to the airport, so she can return home. My elder and other spirit sister's were in shock, we talked gently with her and the initiate decided to try again.

Continued in next post. 

This picture is not from the actual initiation, but a general gut 굿 ceremony.

Setting up an altar is easy, but it requires ritual to purify the space and then placing the proper gods, ancestors and spirits. Then we will activate various house spirits/guardians and earth deities of our home. 

I am a lineage holder of my closed traditions. Spirit mom hopes to pass on her bell rattles. I hope to live up to all their expectations and more, which is why I take my training so seriously.

REPOST @comfortwomenaction
Repost @queenswhorule • A new sculptural group, called "A Heartfelt Apology", is to be installed at Odaesan National Park in Gangwon-do province in Korea this August. 

The installation represents a young Korean girl in early 20th-century dress receiving a man who is bowing on both knees with his forehead to the ground—a type of bow that is only reserved for the deepest of apologies, prayer, and respect for elders. The girl represents the many victims of Japanese imperial violence, while the man represents the conservative Japanese prime minister, Abe Shinzo—visually demonstrating how events in the past shape the lives and experiences of people in the present. 

The sculptor, Wang Gwang Hyun, conceived of this installation to validate experiences of imperial violence, and also make an urgent statement calling on Japan to accept, recognize, and teach their own history. 

To learn more about the story of these young women and girls, and the ways that their experiences as well as imperial violence continue to shape public art across the globe, be sure to watch "When it's not okay to take down a statue," in our Monumental Women series.

For years the family refused to discuss and speak about anything related to the gods or thier history. In the end, the granddaughter had to accept the spirits for her sake, and her family's because her child was sick. 

I know that often spirituality, working with spirits is often painted in glitter, glamour and fluff.
There is power and beauty in the transformations, spiritual rebirth and sure...its sexy but some do not survive. 
Some easily dismiss extreme caution because they never experienced the negative recoil. Eager to play around and experiment with no accountability and no knowledge. 

We have a saying, for every 10 mudangs only 3 are real.  Referring to their spiritual power, training and practice.

This is real talk. Lets cut the sexy glitter fluffy woo woo unicorn poop. 
I know what I say isnt popular, and I am not the authority figure for ALL things Korean Shamanism. But I do know the difference between shit poop and bean paste.

posts.caption:
This may be triggering to some. This story contains murder and family violence. ⁣
⁣
In a rural village, less than an hour outside of Seoul there lived a elderly woman. She was the village mudang, a bosal (a bodhisattva). ⁣Her grandmother before her, was a great manshin of her village as well.

Everyone would come to her for advice. Villagers were often poor and bartered goods like chickens, cows, sacks of rice, sugar, and salt in exchange for the mudangs work. ⁣
She was a strict and dedicated woman devoting her life to the gods and Buddha. She was able to build a small temple for her community,  becoming the shrine keeper. ⁣
She was blessed with many children, and grandchildren but no one wanted to follow in grandma's footsteps. ⁣
For years grandma would try to pass on and teach one of her children, but they all refused and was scared. ⁣
As time grew grandma aged and she worried relentlessly about passing the family gods, ancestral deities and guardian spirits.⁣
Post Korean war, many struggle to survive and times were incredibly difficult. Her oldest son has been pestering his parents to sell the land of the shrine and temple. Many arguments and the parents firmly refused, and relationship was rocky.
⁣
While his father was fetching water from their own private well, he pushed his father down into it. He dragged his mother and locked her in the shrine with no food and water. The mudang grandmother fought relentlessly and her last words was - that Sanshin grandfather (god of the mountain) and his tiger will come for him. ⁣
⁣
3 days later, in a horrific accident the oldest son passed away. News spread like willdfire in the village, and the land was deemed cursed from all the horrors that unfolded. ⁣
Developers came, bought out the land and decided to bulldoze and tear down the shrines. They erect tall apartments buildings but workers began to get sick or die from accidents. Many contractors were scared and buildings took a long time to complete. ⁣
Once residents started to move in, many would get sick or pass away from freak incidents. Rumors started to circulate that the land was haunted by the mudang and her gods. ⁣
⁣
⁣
Continued in the next post.⁣

posts.caption:
Korean Shamanism is political. ⁣
Its been battered, shaped and molded by governing policies for centuries. ⁣
⁣
Shamans were called in to perform rituals and ceremonies in palaces by Kings and Queens. Performing rituals like rain rites, national security, for the country and used as political instruments. 
⁣
In the 1980s, a group of college student banded together to put on a public performance as protest. ⁣
⁣
Madang Kut was adapted as an artful form of political protest, that touched upon the hearts of those who watched.⁣
Performed by students, used as a vechile to deliver a STRONG message of hope and resistance. ⁣
⁣
⁣
As I learn more deeply about our sacred spiritual traditions, couldn't just bypass and dismiss the political histories that has colored our practice, shaping our history and the korean mindset. ⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣pictured: holding a fan and bell rattle, mid jump and mid air, dressed in ceremonial regalia called sinbok 신북 or ui-dae 의대. Jumping to invoke and call down the spirits in a kut ceremony. 
⁣
⁣⁣

When I was first initiated...⁣
I was prohibited from praying the in the mountains. ⁣
⁣
Mountains are hotspots for energies, spirits and low ghosts. For an 애동제자 (a baby disciple) its easy to become influenced by negative spirits because our 'spiritual sight' has opened. ⁣
Being a mudang doesnt protect you from negativity, or low spirits. Because we are with one foot in the physical and the spiritual, we are susceptible to all energies as a spirit pillar. ⁣
⁣
Just how medical doctors have strict procedures and process. It would be horrific if a doctor performed surgery without  sterilizing their equipment or washing their hands. ⁣
The same is for us. ⁣
You would never start a ritual or a rite without clearing the space. And when you finish, a rite to feed the wandering spirits with an exorcism performed to clear. ⁣
The success of a proper exorcism depends on the spiritual ki power of the mudang. If the mudang 'ki' energy is lacking then the exorcism cleansing wont be a succes -becoming a spirit buffet. ⁣
⁣
There is a reason for training that most overlook. ⁣
Our traditions, our culture is the root and stories of our ancestors. 
I think its proper we told our stories correctly- to help release the han of the land, people and us. I think our ancestors deserve that much. 
⁣

posts.caption:
July 17th was CHOBOK 초북. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Sambok 삼북 are 3 days thats considered the hottest during the year. When the yin energy falls and yang energy rises. ⁣⁣
•Chobok 초북 is the 1st hottest day⁣⁣
•Jungbok 중북 2nd hottest day⁣⁣
•Malbok 말북 3rd hottest day.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
The philosophy and concept of Sambok goes back to the Qing dynasty. ⁣⁣
⁣For villages, sambok is welcomed because the heat made the rice grow quickly. ⁣⁣
 ⁣⁣
Traditional foods like gingseng chicken soup is eaten on this day, to promote food health. Ginseng helps fill in lacking nutrition, revitalizing our soul and spirit.⁣⁣
In older times dog meat soup was consumed due to lack of metal energy. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Going on picnics, swimming in rivers, eating watermelons, melons or drinking water from natural wells are all part of the tradition of the Sambok rituals. ⁣⁣
We celebrate this traditions by  honoring our ancestors. ⁣
⁣
❤🙇‍♀️💛 ⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣

I sat under the blanket of stars of the night's sky. Set a small altar with offerings along the mountainside. 

I bowed to the stars, the moon and heavens.
To our spirits, gods, guardians and ancestors. My breath and movement became one, harmonizing the energies around. To channel the energies. 

Prostrating in front of the altar, with each bow I lowered my face down to the grass.

Our spiritual rituals, kut and rites were always performed at night. At the hour of the rat, is when time is fluid - neither yang (male) or yin (female). Its when the energies are changing and transitioning - fluid. 

Night is when yin energy is dominant, most active time for spirits. It is when our ancestors come to visit, peering over us as we sleep. For those who are energy sensitive, a good night sleep is hard to manage.

posts.caption:
Lets talk about initiation, the ritual and gods - because its so needed. ⁣
⁣
First our traditions are - closed,⁣
requires initiation ritual by an elder teacher mudang, manshin. WITH TRAINING!! 
Even the great Master Kim Keum Hwa said that becoming initiated does NOT mean you are a shaman, a mudang. 

⁣Its fascinating to me that some shamans are claiming to work with the gods but have no idea which ancestor spirit is connected. ⁣
똥인지 된장인지 몰라. An old saying that one doesnt know the difference between bean paste and shit poop. 
⁣
you CANNOT bypass an initiation, regardless if you are chosen or a "natural" because an initiation is needed to filter out and send off low energy spirits, ghosts and wandering spirits. ⁣
⁣To work with the gods, to have the gods descent down into you means that the spirit themselves went through a cleansing and initiation. A washing to rid of pollution. ⁣You cant work with the gods (as a shaman) when you dont know which ancestor spirit is seated!! ⁣

Spiritual traditions and teachings are passed down with rituals and sacred knowledge that took centuries to build and perfect.
⁣
I just recently posted about lineages and accountability!! 

I want to ask you, what part of our rich ancient spiritual roots is lacking?⁣
⁣Is your practice really appreciation and not appropriation. You are not preserving  traditions, you are sanitizing and washing it down. We diasporas are conditioned by the western world, that we are entited to it. 

So much destruction, look at the Native Am of the stolen land still fighting for their rights. Spiritual practices are taken exploited and appropriated without paying the proper respect!!! Same for Hoodoo traditions, and other indigenous spiritual traditions.

Sorry not sorry⁣

This body of mine is literally a temple, a conduit that allows me to work in my spiritual traditions. ⁣⁣

I was reminded of who I am, a strong fucking woman with a lineage of powerful ancestors behind me. ⁣⁣

REPOST 
from @wildbodysomatics 🌌 

Recent calls from multiple BIPOC lead networks and individuals within healing justice work have been powerfully naming the harm that can be done when someone is practicing without training, lineage, and accountability. For white practitioners in particular this is a way we often continue enacting extractive and apppropriative colonial dynamics within healing and wellness communities. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
Asking about someone’s training is less about having specific certifications and more about practitioners knowing our own nervous systems and embodying our values- or knowing when we have stopped doing these things bc we are human and it happens all the time- and having ways to bring ourselves back to presence and connection. For white folks in particular it is about unlearning urgency and domination. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
These are not all my original ideas, I have only assembled them. The concept of lineage is deeply rooted in healing justice. Let this be a moment to really listen to what that means in practice.

Some questions you might ask: ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
Does this person have the capacity to ground and resource (or regulate if that’s your language)? How do you feel in your body when you are with them? (An initial consult or the first session is a great way to check this out). ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
How have they trained to do this work? Have they personally taken part in the modality they are offering? How many years have they been in practice before holding space for others? (A minimum of 5 years is a good start) Do they have mentors, teachers, others who offer guidance and support in their work? ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
What lineages do they practice in? What are their relationships to these lineages? to their teachers, the cultural context of the teachings, are they in a practice of being in right relationship to this lineage?(Paying reparations, acknowledging where practices come from)⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
Who are their communities and who are they accountable to? Can you talk to someone who has worked with them? Is there a demonstration of humility in how they approach their work? ⁣⁣⁣Does this person have a process in place for addressing harm and accountability if necessary?

posts.caption:
KUT 굿 is a Korean shamanic ceremony and ritual, often involving grand and elaborate altars, abundant offerings, paper goods, the descent and trance possession of the gods and the spirits of the ancestors. Listed below are some of the kuts that is commonly performed. 

▪︎재수굿 Jesu-kut, a ceremony to bring prosperity, luck and abundance. The god of wealth, fortune and business 대감 Daegam is important in this type of ritual, and require meat offerings to Daegam. Mostly performed for businesses, to bring in luck and prosperity. 
▪︎병굿 byeong-kut, ceremony to aid in sickness and disease. The gods of longevity,  medicine, the General and their officers also play crucial roles.
▪︎49제  is a Buddhist inspired ritual involving the spirit/soul of the recently departed. After 49 days of their death, this ritual helps aid and washing of spirits impurities to enter the spirit world. 
▪︎진옥이 굿 jinogwi-kut, this ceremony is meant to guide the spirit and soul of the deceased that hasn't departed. Spirits that missed their chance and now stuck here, wandering and hungry ghosts. Helping release grievances, han and the washing of the spirit. After the spirit is guided back, we unveil ritual tools that reveal reincarnation. Sometimes we can see imprint of a bird, or the body of a dog, prints of a bear, etc that hints on their reincarnation.

 There are too many types of kut ceremony within our traditions. These are just some of the kut ceremony that my lineage actively performs here in the US.

posts.caption:
In the lunar month of July, a few important sacred holidays  coming up. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Chilseok day falls on the 7th day of the 7th lunar month. Its a day of celebration performed by mudangs, villagers and the community. ⁣⁣
•Celebration includes the mythical story of two lovers separated by the milky way. ⁣
•Women praying to the goddess for more beautiful embroidery needlework. ⁣⁣
•Rituals to encourage crops and field to grow⁣⁣
•Most importantly, its a day to pay respect and reverance to Chilseong, the 7 stars of the Ursa Major Big Dipper constellation. I've written about this ritual every year when we perform it. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
 ⁣⁣
Later on we celebrate our version of 'All Souls Day' similar to the Mexican festival of 'Dias de Meurtes'. When the gates of the spirit world open, and we commemorate the dead, the spirits and our ancestors. A ritual of to purify the village is perform to protect the community from calamities. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Its very important folk holiday and said to be on the verge of extinction and no longer practiced as a community.
⁣⁣Looking forward to celebrating these deeply rooted traditions. Stay tuned, will share more information as the days comes. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
⁣
Pictured is my spirit mom, my elder and my teacher. Yes, its important to know our roots and traditions but what she really taught me is to uphold our work with integrity and honor.

We have a Native elder living on the reservation near Albuquerque, NM. ⁣
⁣
Bob (as we call him) is the medicine man and elder for the tribe and reservation of the Jicarilla Apache. ⁣
Bob is also the direct descendant of Geronimo, a famous prominent leader and medicine man of the Apache. ⁣
⁣
The tribe is taking down their old teepee (dilapidated) which was built in the 1980s The teepee is used for ritual and ceremonial, particularly for their crown dancers. ⁣
⁣
The tribe needs to build a new tipi for their ritual and ceremonies, and also for their crown dancers. The building of the tipi is incredibly sacred. ⁣
⁣
Bob is like family to me, because he is family to my spirit sister Mia. ⁣
We are not indigenous or native, but refer to each other as brother and sister. ❤🙏⁣
⁣
We been trying to put together funds to help Bob and his tribe achieve building their teepee. ⁣

Tomorrow (6/25) is Dano Festival Day. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Its actually a major shamanic holiday, with roots of sun and sky worshipping. A day when yang energy is at the highest and strongest.

⁣⁣
Women washed their hair in changpo (sweet flag) essence makes their hair shiny. Women put essential oils of the female ginseng plant in their hair, hoping the fragrance would ward off evil.⁣⁣

posts.caption:
In our Korean traditions, there are many types of spiritual professionals like the shaman, the mudang. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
To list a few:⁣⁣
• Pansu often blind, an exorcist and divinator working with spirits of the Earth. ⁣⁣
•Bosal/Posal can be initiated but their spiritual power isnt seen as strong as the mudang. Can also be used to refer to a mudang, a cross between a Buddhist nun and mudang. ⁣
•Baksu are male mudangs⁣⁣
•Popsa/Beobsa can be initiated but will train specifically in the sutras, hymns, oral epics, gori's of a kut ritual. May speacialize in the 'sitting ritual' of anjeongeori. ⁣⁣Well versed in the traditional instruments and music. ⁣⁣
These are just a few of the professional spiritual practioners other than a mudang.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣

posts.caption:
The virgin goddess worshipped by a fishing village. ⁣
⁣
애바위 which refers to the rock, the boulder where the young betrothed female was last seen. Her shrine is called 해신당 Haesindang, which has turned into a park with penis sculptures. ⁣
⁣
One version of her story says that she was standing on a rock, while her fiancee was fishing. A storm came sweeping her away.⁣
Another version says that she jumped into the sea to save her fisherman fiancee.⁣
⁣
After her death, the villagers werent able to catch any fishes. Then one day a man peed into the ocean, and villagers believed that the male organ appeased her anger.  Penises were built all over to placate her anger  and to receive bountiful harvest from the ocean. ⁣
⁣
• • • • • •⁣
⁣
She is a goddess revered by the local people. ⁣
Spirit mom took us to her shrine as she taught me the difference between the types of spirits. ⁣
A virgin spirit is seen as wrathful due to unfulfilling important milestones such as marriage.⁣
⁣
One researcher said that the virgin maiden is actually another goddess of the ocean. This ocean goddess aids the villagers with bountiful harvest of fish. ⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣⁣
⁣
⁣
Pictures from Google ⁣
Had no time to take pictures of my own⁣

Last year, we were able to capture a heartbreaking and inspirational story of Ji-Hwan, who, despite his own financial struggles raising his daughter on his own, was running an organization to help other single fathers in Korea. ⁣
⁣
⁣

⁣
I grew up with a single father, we had help from the family.⁣
But I am a child of a single parent. ⁣
Growing up in the 90s almost unheard of that a father has custody of his children. ⁣

posts.caption:
노무편 Nomupyeon (Old Shaman) is the earliest written mention of the 무당 mudang (shaman) in Korean text. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
Written by 이규보 Yi Gyobo a Confucian scholar during the Goryeo dynasty. The poem he wrote expressed his delighted joy when the neighborhood  shaman was expelled, and clearly shows - how much Confucianism despised shamanism. ⁣
One part, Yi marvelled at⁣⁣ "how is she able to live this long". ⁣⁣⁣
⁣
Yi's poem, gives detailed discussion of the shamanic activities, views and attitudes of the people towards shamanism. A crucial piece of evidence that gives detailed accounts of the shaman mudang activities. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
• • • • • • • • •⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
I have the English translated version of the "Old Shaman" poem by 이규보. ⁣⁣⁣
If anyone is interested, I can do a live video, possibly reading and having a mini discussion about it. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
Trying something new⁣⁣⁣
Let me know. ⁣⁣⁣
🤩🤗⁣⁣⁣

posts.caption:
In honor of Asian Pacific Islander Hertiage Month and Children's Day 어린이날. ⁣
⁣
Children's Day (May 5) is a holiday in Korea honoring children, started by an activist in 1923 during the time of the Japanese occupation.  As oppression grew, later 어린이날 was banned by the Japanese in 1939. ⁣
⁣
After the Korea War, celebration of 어린이날 resumed. ⁣
⁣
Mother's Day also started sometime in the 1930s and later changed to Parents Day to show equality towards fathers. ⁣
⁣
⁣
• • • • •⁣
⁣
⁣
I dont have much pictures of myself as a baby or growing child. When my parents divorced, my father in his raging kimchi temper threw out our albums.⁣ ⁣
Growing up, I was constantly subjected to head shaving. One head shaving occasion, I was gifted a wig. Apparently I hated the itchy and scratchy wig, that I threw it down  completely embarrassing my mother. ⁣
⁣
In preschool, my head was shaved again but this time I was given an entire new wardrobe. My mother dressed me up as a boy, and I loved it. ⁣I remember dressing up in boys clothing and feeling like I was given a superhero cape. As if it was permission to run wild, cause mishcief and play like the "boys". ⁣
⁣
⁣Looking back...my mother often says alot of my childhood events foreshadowed the telling of my becoming into a mudang. ⁣
⁣
⁣
Head shaving was very common to do, still practiced by some. An old wives tale, to promote hair thickness and growth. ⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣

posts.caption:
개양 할미 Gaeyang Halmi⁣
⁣
is the Ocean goddess, ruler of the West sea (Yellow Sea) - indigenous to Korea. Gaeyang Halmi ruled the sea with her 8 daughters. ⁣⁣⁣
소성당 (Suseongdang)the shamanic shrine located in Buan, Jeolla-bukdo. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
Its said that 개양 할미 was the protective sea goddess that provided safe passage and the protection for the fisherman. The coastal western sea is known for its turbulent and choppy waters, and the goddess is worshipped for her ability control the sea and the winds that affects the currents. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
Most of her daughters - except the youngest were married and were sent away to other islands and provinces. The goddess is said to be so big and massive that she travels the sea by walking on wooden shoes, controlling the depths of the oceans by filling up the deepest parts.⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
The villagers and shamans still conduct their yearly ritual to the Geayang Halmi Goddess.  Its said and believed that the goddess came from the sea through a dragon cave nearby the shrine [pic 2]. The dragon cave is believed to have 24 hyeol energy centers, its inaccessible due to the rising waters. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
⁣
⁣
More so than often the ocean gods and deities are depicted as males. Goddess of the Ocean and the sea arent as well known. ⁣
 Spirit mom took us to this shrine, explicitly explaining the importance of this goddess. ⁣⁣⁣
I was very fortunate to have visited this sacred place and making a connection. I still clearly remember the visions I had while in ritual at the shrine. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣

posts.caption:
The flag of 고려 Goryeo or Koryo, the Korean kingdom founded in 918.⁣⁣
Goryeo period was known for the Golden Age for Buddhism, achieving the highest influence. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
In the text 'History of the Koryo' a number of references are made about the shaman. Its the official record for the history of the Koryo period. Many occasions the King gathered shamans, having them pray and perform rain rituals. ⁣⁣
One account states that a horse (expensive, only reserved for rich top rank officials) was given as payment for a ceremony. Shaman were not tax-exempt and required to pay taxes in rolls of hemp cloth. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Ancient records indicate that mountain spirits were originally great goddesses. Its during this Koryo period, mountain gods were changed to male and the patriarchal influence is still present in Korean shamanism. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣The flag center with the bird. ⁣
Birds are shamanic emblem because it refers to flight towards the Heavens, like the shaman soul or spirit. ⁣
⁣⁣
⁣
⁣

Mago Halmoni 마고할머니, the Giant Earth Goddess 🌎💜.⁣⁣

마고 carried mud in her skirt, and she used to create the mountains and islands. With her urine excrement she formed hills and rivers. ⁣⁣

Mago is credited for  geographical formation of nature. 마고 creation myth was reduced to just a folktale and often overlooked. The story of 마고 is passed down orally and omitted from formal worship of state rituals and studies. ⁣⁣

The creation story of Mago is from 관북 province in present-day North Korea. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣

⁣⁣

posts.caption:
The earliest landscape painting unearthed from the Korean peninsula revealed (near Pyongyang) Korea's own Goddess of love, beauty, and immortality. ⁣
⁣
The goddess is known as So wang-mo 소왕모, Fairy Queen of the Western Sea, Fairy Peach and even Seonyeo.  She grows a peach tree on a mountain top in her Jade palace besides Jasper Lake.  The tree leaves bud, growing every 3,000 years and taking another 3,000 years for the peach to ripen. ⁣
⁣
When the goddess isn't painted, she's symbolized by her peaches, the fruit of immortality. ⁣
⁣
소왕모 is also known as the Queen Mother of the West, and in the Chinese culture, she is known as Xi Wangmu with Daoist orgins, known as the wife of the Jade Emperor. ⁣
The 3rd son of King Sejong in 1447, dreamt of the peach orchard of 소왕모. A painter was summoned to create the dream vision for the Prince drawn on silk. ⁣
⁣
There are famous Korean art pieces showcasing the "Banquet of Sowangmo (XiWangmu)" from the Joseon Dynasty. ⁣
⁣
The 2nd picture shows 소왕모 with her maiden helper from the Goguryeo Kingdom period, as noted by the National Museum of Korea.⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣

posts.caption:
There are many types of paintings depicting gods in various styles. If you look closely and observe the symbolism, it tells a story. ⁣
⁣
In these shamanic portraits of Sanshin 산신 god of mountain, the deity is holding a white feathered fan. A symbol noting back to the mythology of Danggun (the grandson of Heavens). ⁣
White feather fans are usually connected to the white crane. The crane is symbolic for nobility, emblem rank for government officials. A longevity symbol known for its regal, integrity and its sagacity wisdom.  The white crane is a spiritual and holy symbol for its magic and magical essence of longevity. ⁣
When Sanshin is shown with a white feather fan, its referring to Sanshin authority to command the wind. Sanshin is god of mountain, the earth and guardian of all within. Sanshin authority ties back to the myth of Danggun (the grandson of Heavens- Hwanin). Hwanung (Danggun father) descended from the Heavens with the god of rain, wind and cloud under his command. ⁣
Danggun transformed and turned into Sanshin.⁣
⁣
Some times feathers are also used as ritual tools during ceremony, or used as altar items. Hats are adorned with feathers referring to the mudang shaman ability of flight, traveling within the realms of the upper, middle and lower. ⁣
⁣
⁣
Check out this yeo-sanshin, the female mountain god. ⁣The flowing fabric drawn behind her - another indicator of flight. ⁣
⁣
⁣

posts.caption:
What is a dolmen? ⁣
They are stone tombs, altars and or memorials built with side walls supporting a flat stone on top. They were built sometime during the Neolithic period (1000 BCE) and some later. ⁣
⁣
In Korea, they are called "goindol" which literally means propped stone.⁣
Some dolmens contains remains of high status individuals, buried with all their bronze goods of daggers, bells, swords, pots, etc. ⁣
⁣
Scholars say that some of those buried in the Dolmens belonged to powerful tribal chiefs and/or shamans. One historian says the side stone walls represents Earth, while the top stone slab represents the sky (Heavens). People believed their chieftains souls resided between where Heaven and Earth met. ⁣
⁣
Another nickname for Korea is the Kingdom of Dolmens. 
40% of the worlds doleman are concentrated just in Korea with over 30,000 plus more found. Most Dolmens in urbanized areas were destroyed for development, and not protected.⁣
⁣
⁣
• • • • •⁣
⁣
Dictionary.com ⁣
defines dolmens as chiefly being found in France and Britain. (Being colonizers have its perks)⁣
Dolmens are found throughout the world, NOT chiefly found in France or Britain. ⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣
