Tonight, I am  missing my spirit mother, my dear elder. ⁣
⁣
It takes me less than 10 minutes to reach  her home. When I enter, I pay my respects to her gods first immediately bowing in the shrine.  Then I make my way greeting all the elders, asking if they all had a restful sleep with a cheerful good morning. ⁣
Sometimes spirit dad makes a smoothie - it looks like the 'grey stuff' from Disney Beauty & Beatst and its a warm!!!! 😑 Made with boiled onions, and all sorts of healthy god-knows-what. Haha. I usually hold my breath and gulp it down, smile respectfully, while I sternly turn down a second portion. ⁣
We always gather for a late breakfast, and I wait till every elder took a bite of their food, before I take mine. (Its how I was raised, but how I want to express my respect). I'm not a person for emotional words, instead I show through my actions big or small. ⁣
⁣
We spend all day together. Spirit dad would tell me the same stories again, and often we chatter up a storm. I've been told curiosity kills the cat. Whenever I see spirit mom, I overload her with many pondering questions that I try to be mindful not to abuse. I always start with...mom, can I ask a question ? Which she replies always. ⁣
⁣
Its been 5 or so weeks since I seen my spirit mother and I miss her. I call everyday to make sure everyone is okay. I nag to them, making sure they stay home, and volunteer to help with groceries and errands. ⁣
⁣

I was told by someone yesterday I need to share more. ⁣

posts.caption:
How did politics affect the Mudang and Korean Shamanism? ⁣
⁣
The ancient kings of Korea were often called different titles that referred to them as a shaman. Kings of Korea were seen as head shamans, leading rituals to worship the sun, the mountain, calling in the rain and performing exorcism rituals to appease malicious spirits.⁣
⁣
Buddhism and Confucianism was imported in the 4th Century.  While surrounding ancient nations adopted Buddhism but Silla held onto her shamanistic roots for another century before succumbing. ⁣
⁣
During the Joseon period (heavily Confucius) mudang were prohibited from entering the city (Hanyang, now Seoul). Mudangs were classified as dirty and the lowest social class. Hefty taxes and heavy fines was slapped on a mudang to deter their practices. ⁣
Its during this time, shamanism became the religion of the woman. ⁣
Its during a kut 굿 ceremony that women were allowed freely to express themselves in a repressed Confucian society.  Drinking, singing, dancing and releasing all the stress of a repressed life.⁣
During the Japanese Occupation, Mugyo or Musok was seen as dirty and lowclass. The Japanese attempted to replace Korean Shamanism with their Shinto. ⁣
⁣
A brutal blow to Korean shamanic roots was during "New Village Movement" (Saemaeul-ho Undong). Initiated in the 70s by President Park to eradicate anything that resembled shamanism. Most shrines and temples in rural countryside and elsewhere were torn down. A modern 'enlightened' movement to bring Korea to westernized. ⁣
⁣
⁣
And we survived. ⁣
Grew back stronger⁣
because our roots are too deep to ignore. ⁣
We come from a land of survival. ⁣
Our ancestors were badass survivors, who birthed and gave life to us. ⁣
We are a product of an amazing and resilient ancestral lineage. ⁣
💜✊⁣

posts.caption:
Do you know the story of Korea's last Queen, Empress Myeongseong - Queen Min. ⁣⁣
She came from a powerful clan that had birthed previous Queens. But by the time she was a child, her clan had fallen and she was orphaned. At age 16, she married Gojong. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Her authority as Queen was shaken when the Kings consort birthed a son while Queen Min was childless. Then 20, she finally became pregnant and birthed a son. The baby was ill and needed treatment but passed away. ⁣⁣
She hired shamans and brought mudangs into the palace to find the root cause of her son's untimely passing. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Queen Min association and relationship with mudangs ran deep. She would often sponsor kut 굿 ceremony/ritual. Even at one point, she adopted a mudang as her daughter, a princess. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
I been researching and digging into the Mudang princess. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Queen Min was assassinated by Korean and Japanese assassins due to her opposition against Japanese. They stormed into the Queens quarter, assaulting the women. The assassin took body, burned it and scattered her ashes. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Her marriage with the King was rocky and political, but over time they grew deep love. The King ordered to search for her body, and a funeral was held. He built wooden horses to escort the nation's beloved Queen to the afterworld. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
[In my research, they say that no one really knew what Queen Min looked like, and a portrait was drawn based on their presumptions of what she looked like. Only very few people knew the identity of Queen Min, even her assassin had a hard time]⁣
⁣
⁣⁣
⁣
Side note: alot of details were omitted due to the extreme violence. I did not want to trigger anyone. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Inspired by my conversation with @leedoyun . Thank you. ⁣

posts.caption:
Cheo-yong 처용, The Home guardian against illness and disease. ⁣
⁣
One story says King Heongang 49th King of Silla (9th Century) went to pray at the shrine to the Dragon King of the Eastern sea. Pleased with the Kings tribute the Dragon king ordered his 7 sons to shamanically dance and sing songs. One of his sons stayed behind, to serve the royal as a shaman. ⁣The king arranged for Cheo-yong to marry a beautiful woman as his wife. ⁣
⁣
The god of smallpox plague Yeoksin heard about Cheo-yong wife and desired her. One account says Yeoksin shapeshifted and Cheoyong found them together in bed. Cheoyong began to sing poetically. ⁣
⁣
As translated by Peter Lee in the Analogy of Korean Poetry, a verse in the Song of Cheoyong - "having caroused far in the night. In the moonlight capital I return home and in my bed, Behold 4 legs. Two have been mine, whose the other two? Two have been mine, but no no they are taken". ⁣
⁣
Most ancient stories say the god of plague was impressed by Cheoyong song. Yeoksin surrendered and swore never to enter the home where Cheoyong resides. ⁣
⁣
Thus Cheoyong became defied as a gate god, or door god munsin 문신. Usually on the door frame, a picture of Cheoyong is hung as a form of a talisman/amulet accompanied by a bundle of thorny castor oil stems. Used to deter negativity and have exorcism properties. ⁣
⁣
The song and dance of Cheoyong called Cheoyongmu is one of the oldest court ritual designated as UNESCO Cultural Heritage. ⁣
The dancers features red masks (dispel evil) and colored robes associated with the 4 cardinal direction with the center (yellow), red (south), white (west), black (north) and blue (east). ⁣
⁣
⁣⁣
Late Koryo period different version of  Cheoyong songs appeared serving as a basis for ritual exorcism, chasing away the Plague god. ⁣
⁣ ⁣

posts.caption:
For centuries our Korean ancestors lived harmoniously with the land. ⁣⁣
When spring comes, we tap into Birch or Maple trees collecting its water. We call this precious water 고로쇠 gorosoe which means 'good for bones'. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Luckily we have those trees at my mom's Catskills home. My kids and family enjoy drinking the surprisingly sweet water. If you enjoy coconut water, you will definitely love it. Its love from the land, the earth, trees, our ancestors. ⁣⁣
⁣
⁣
Trees are very sacred in Korean spiritual beliefs, some trees are guardians protecting a village, or a home. Birch trees are even more sacred with Korea's founder descended from the Heavens. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
To show respect, give offerings of makgeolli (korean rice wine), soju (korean liquor) or any liquor on hand. We say that one should not carelessly disturb the tree, so we give offerings as respect. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣

posts.caption:
I remember looking up to a vivid blue sky, with clouds dotted across. ⁣
A majestic white horse with wings flew and weaved in between the clouds.⁣
⁣
Then I woke up, and stayed up all night wondering about the dreams meaning. I was anxious to phone my spirit mum to tell her about it. ⁣
In Korean mythology, the Chollima is a mythical white horse with majestic wings at its sides, like a Korean pegasus. Only difference with the Korean Chollima is that this horse had smaller wings on each hoof like the Roman Mercury god with his winged feet. ⁣
The Chollima, is a mythical horse capable of lightning speed. It desired to become tamed, but no man was able to and instead flew up into the sky, never seen again. ⁣
⁣
The white horse is symbolic and very important to the surrounding areas of North Asia like Mongolia, Tuvan, Tibetan, N.Korea etc. ⁣
⁣
⁣
Spirit mom was happy and pleased to hear about my dream. She shared her wisdom and teachings, which is a very personal message for me. ⁣
⁣
⁣picture take at Ohdae Mountain in Korea. ⁣

The gods of the shaman world. ⁣
⁣
Our gods are spirits -the guardians of the natural heavenly and gods of the humanly world. ⁣
⁣
Gods of the natural world like the stars, sun, moon, mountain, earth, trees, rivers, oceans, etc. Gods of the human world like Kings, Queens, prince, princesses, ancestors, army generals, etc. ⁣
Long before the influences of Confucianism, Buddhism, political and patriarchy. The gods of the shaman natural world were original female. Sanshin 산신 the god of mountain, often depicted as a sagely old man with a long white beard with his majestic tiger - was female. ⁣
There are many ways a mountain is labeled or identified with a god. For example, Jiri Mountain is known as yeo-sanshin (female sanshin) because the physical appearance of the mountain isnt rocky with craggy peaks like Seorak or Taebak mountains. ⁣

posts.caption:
달래 Dahle ⁣
⁣
Korean wild chives or known as mountain chives called dahle.  Same family as garlic, onions and shallots. ⁣
Its symbolic for the incoming spring, and part of the 5 spicy vegetables called oshinchae - and considered a vegetable with  5 virtues.⁣
Its one of the spring vegetables that was offered to the king as tribute. Even a korean folk song sung since the Joseon dynasty tells the story of children running around eating peppers and dahle while dad went out. ⁣
⁣
Dahle was used as folk medicine- as a means to stimulate a person's appetite.  Dahle had uncanny ability to break through the frozen soil, and was eaten to give our ancestors vitality and strength. ⁣
⁣
Mom foraged these right in our yard, growing naturally and abundantly. ⁣
⁣
⁣

posts.caption:
In remembrance of the Seoul's March 1st Movement. The first public movement against the Japansese occupation of Korea. ⁣
⁣
A momumental moment in Korea's history with the release of The March First Declaration of Independence at Pagoda Park, much of this was due to the efforts of women. Read more about the real story of the March 1st movement in book called Pumpkin Flower and Patriotism by Kyung Soo Cha. ⁣(source: Dosan Ahn Chang Ho FB page). ⁣
Woman were not seen as threat by the Japanese but Mudangs were. Mudangs were a threat to the Japanese because mudangs is symbolic, the epitome of Korean culture and history, raising morale and patriotism. ⁣
The significance of the nam chima (blue skirt). Its an essential piece of spirit clothing regalia (sinbok). Most mudangs were driven underground, shamanizing in secrecy. Mudangs wore their nam chima in a silent protest against the Japanese. ⁣
⁣

My maternal grandparents were farmers and business merchants. They knew how to work and cultivate the land -farmers, which meant they worked closely with spirits,  gods and the deities. 
Immigrating to the US in the late 80s, early 90s. Working with other Korean elders, they turned a local dump into a bustling farm co-op in NYC. ⁣⁣⁣

If you are on a picnic, or happen to eat your meal outside. Before you eat, take a little piece of our food and throw in the air 3 times while saying GOSURE or GOSURI.⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
Grandma said this was just a simple and humble way of paying respect to spirits. The spirits, they eat first. ⁣⁣I remember her teachings, and when I have a picnic or a meal. I throw pieces of food yelling GOSURE GOSURE GOSURE 고수레. ⁣⁣⁣its seen as a respectful gesture of feeding the land, or wandering spirits. ⁣⁣⁣⁣
Thanking my grandmother for teaching me her wisdom. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣

With the explosion of the spiritual community and seekers, there are alot of misunderstandings of many things. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
I can't tell you how many times I've had people that they set and built altars, but things are going badly. Experiencing nightmares, insomnia, bad luck and misfortune the list goes on. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
A word of advice is, please dont take it lightly. Once you set an altar it will be difficult to dispose of, and the method is quite involved and complicated. If you are NOT confident about the upkeep, maintenance and other duties involved...then its better not to set up. ⁣I'm referring to home altars, not ancestral jesa offering altars which are different. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣
I know a woman, whose mother threw out the spirit house and altar. Eventually bringing bad luck and demise to the family, as each one member was picked off with an unfortunate circumstance. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣
Thank you Steph for the amazing gift.  I love my handmade broom ❤⁣ And for stopping by for a visit all the way from the west coast. Love the broom- a craft, a skill that is close to my heart. ⁣⁣

posts.caption:
The Great Full Moon offerings of dried vegetables and bean varieties. ⁣
⁣
Are you guys sick and tired of all the 대보름 Dae-Boreum posts? ⁣
⁣
The traditional food and offerings used are all dried. Dried vegetables are used, dried beans are used and dried nuts in shells (not pictured) are used. ⁣
⁣
What is the importance of all this? When I peer deeper into the rich symbolism of our animistic roots, its all about interconnection, symbolic for the cycles of life. By being part of the cycle, we are one with the natural world. ⁣
⁣
Chuseok Mid Autumn Festival is very important because of the bounty we receive. With Dae-Boreum we prepare to welcome the Spring Season which signifies new growth and life from the budding of plants and trees, after a period of resting in the Winter. ⁣
Following (as best as I can) our ancestral traditions and customs allows me to appreciate and give gratitude to the various cycles within our lives, in ways our ancestors did. Walking within this practice and lifestyle has helped broaden and deepen my understanding of our history, ancestors and our own personal journeys. ⁣
⁣
⁣

posts.caption:
Great Full Moon (Dae-Boreum) divination. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
The Korean Lunar Full Moon is such an important day of festivals and rituals. Various types of divination is performed by all to predict the upcoming fortune for the year.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
A moon house is built by the community and set on fire. ⁣
•If the Moon House falls or tops over a certain direction, its interpreted to forecast prosperity. ⁣⁣
•If the smoke from the Moon House is so thick and covers the moon, seen as a great omen. ⁣⁣
•The color and the brightness of the Moon is also observed for divination ⁣⁣
•Cows are given special feed mixed rice porridge with different beans. If the cow eats the rice first, then it forecast great rice agriculture, if beans are eaten other crops will flourish. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
These are just some of the divination types that were used by the Korean people and ancestors. The first Lunar Full Moon is such an important evil chasing ritual festival that sets the tone for the upcoming year, helps people prepare. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣
What it means - we were always in contact and in communication with the natural world. We give offerings, cleansing and raise the 'spirits energy'. Achieving balance with the spiritual and the humanly. ⁣

posts.caption:
Great 🌕 Full Moon Festival  Dae-Boreum 대보름. Also a day of folk magic and rituals. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
This auspicious day is spent strengthening bonds and ties with your neighbors and the community.  Its a time when the community and villagers unify to participate, working with one another for the peace and well-being of the village or community. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣ A Earth ritual of Jisin-bapgi 지신밟기 means to 'Step on Earth' which a folk ritual dedicated to the land, Earth goddess or land spirit called Jisin 지신. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Purpose of this ritual is to being prosperity,  chasing away negativity and expelling evil with the loud percussion of the drums and gongs. While they sing and chant good wishes. The  band would also visit the surrounding homes spreading cheer, blessings and chasing away negativity. Homeowners would come out to greet the band with food, drinks and money. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
A moon house (spirit house or pillar) called Dal-jip 달집 is built by the community. Children and adults would write their wishes and tie it to the branches of the moon house. As the full moon rises, the moon house is set on fire,  a sacred fire meant to bring in blessings. The louder the fire crackles means the greater the "exorcism" as it cleanse and purifies. Like how firecrackers are used to chase evil, expelling negative forces. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣
I hope to one day to have a space for rituals, prayers and moon houses. ❤ community. ⁣⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣

posts.caption:
The Great Full Moon known as Dae-Boreum 대보름 is Saturday, Feb 8th. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
If you are setting up offerings for this full moon, then I will share the traditional and customary foods used on a special day like the Great Full Moon. ⁣⁣⁣
Customary offerings are:⁣⁣⁣
•Nuts in the shell like walnuts and peanuts. ⁣⁣⁣
•Special dried vegetables called 보름 나물 Boreum-Namul means Great Full Moon Vegetables. ⁣Taro stem, dried pumpkin,  sweet potato stems,  dried eggplant, dried fernbracken (gosari). ⁣⁣
•Special mixed rice with various beans called Ogok-bap  오곡밥⁣ ⁣⁣or yak-bap 약밥 which is glutinous rice cakes with dates, chestnuts, pine nuts with honey. ⁣⁣The commoners used ogok-bap but the wealthy aristocrats had yakbap. ⁣
⁣
Dae-Boreum is also a day, when people visit a mudang, to take part in a effigy doll cleansing exorcism called Hongsu-maegi. ⁣⁣⁣
There are many spiritual and folk symbolism on this Dae-Boreum. Which I will share some of the folk divination, magic and customs the next coming posts.⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣

Gasin House spirits. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Villages were built and positioned near mountains and rivers for their sacred energies. Village and homes are sacred, as they are part of the sacred nature surrounding them, as an extension. ⁣
⁣
Our homes are sacred, provides us with shelter for our families. Children are born, and sacred life event happens within the home.⁣ ⁣
⁣⁣
A small offering to the kitchen goddess Jowangsin and to the home. We gave our house spirits - gratitude and prayers for the family and New Year. 🙏🙇‍♀️⁣ ⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣
In older times, Koreans believed mischievous glowing ghosts would descend to steal one's shoes. To protect their shoes from the shoe-stealing ghosts 👠👻... people hung up baskets, or sieves. The ghost will become enchanted and so preoccupied by counting the holes in the sieve and basket till morning. If your shoes were stolen it meant the victim of shoe theft will not receive any blessings or luck. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
These ghosts appears the night before the Lunar New Year and before the night of the first Full Moon. So hide your shoes. 😄⁣⁣
⁣⁣

posts.caption:
Happy Lunar New Year 🎉⁣
We call this celebration, Seollal 설날. Its a family holiday celebrating the 1st day of the Lunar Metal Rat Year. ⁣
⁣
Spent all day cooking, and luckily my partner was home to help assist me. Fruit, liquor, water, vegetables, fritters, rice cakes, meat, fish, desserts and traditional snacks was all laid out. ⁣
⁣
Most important offering of 떡국 ttuk-guk (rice cake soup) a traditional dish eaten on Seollal. The eating a bowl of ttuk-guk symbolizes good health and growing a year older. Its thought that this customary practice originated in ancient times. During the Goryeo period it was one of the major holidays to pay worship to ones ancestors. ⁣
⁣
Its also customary for communities to visit their local mudang (shaman) to participate in exorcism and cleansing ritual prayers. For some families, an important part of their customs as it drives away any negative influences protecting them for the new year. ⁣
⁣
All those who submitted their names for candles, I created a separate table. For each candle lit, we rubbed our hands in prayer prostration and bowed. Thank you for all the candle  submissions. ⁣
⁣
Wishing everyone a blessed and happy Lunar New Year. ⁣

posts.caption:
Today's kut ceremony ritual felt like a rug was pulled out underneath me. ⁣
⁣
For the last few months I been withdrawing more and putting all my efforts into studying. There is so much to my training, that at times its feels endless. When I have such an amazing spirit mom as a role model, its inspiring.  My biggest life obstacle is myself, I lack confidence. ⁣
⁣
But today during the kut ceremony....⁣
Daeshin Halmoni 대신할머니 (The Great Spirit Grandmother) was invoked and descended into spirit mother. She sang her songs and oral epics, she gave gongsu 공수 (divine channelled messages) to the client, Mrs. Coco (not real name).⁣
⁣
Daesin spoke about the hardship about her, Mrs Coco life and the destiny that is attached. Then Daesin looked around the room with us and said look at each one of you, everyone has a heavy and sad destiny. ⁣
⁣
Daeshin walked up to me, and said Look at you, isnt life hard and cold? Its really hard isnt it...walking this path and raising a young family. (I was startled by my own tears.) You often want to shut down from the world, but what are you gonna do? Did you forget, your destiny was already created from the gods and Heaven (sky). Just like your spirit mother, this is the only path for you...just this only. So do your best. Your gods, they know, they see and understand. ⁣
⁣
By then the tears just streamed down like waterfalls and still is as I am writing this. Daeshin knew my heart, acknowledge and understood me. That was worth everything.  She also gave me the push and inspiration to move forward, that I can do this. ⁣
⁣
It really is everything to me and I am so thankful today. ⁣
⁣
⁣

posts.caption:
Last 2 days have been incredibly tough. The spiritual energies of the upcoming kut ceremony has me really messed up. Stomach has been a big issue, feels like a giant boulder is sitting on me. No amount of medicine provides any relief, and an exorcism is only temporary because of the Kut ceremony related energies. ⁣
⁣
As always... with any ceremony, sleep is elusive but its the JIGI that always proves to be difficult. ⁣
⁣
What is JIGI then? ⁣
Hard to describe, but will try my best to explain. Jigi is like an empathic ability but on a more intense level. Usually a person's ancestors or even their own spiritual energy gets transferred onto me. Jigi is another form of storytelling and communication, it allows me to 'walk in someone else's shoes'. ⁣
For instance,  I had someone visit me and as soon as the person walked in my shrine. I felt I was blindsided with an immense pain on the left side of my head -a migraine. Never had one, and now I sympathize. ⁣
Just last night,  I was preparing for a session and while sipping some hot tea...I managed to spill the hot contents all over myself. I was dumbstruck by my actions, then realizing I must be getting jigi from the client which was comfirmed. ⁣
⁣
Having jigi is difficult, because at times I cant tell if I am really sick or if its the spiritual energies. Before or even during a kut, there's been cases where the jigi we receive was severe that we have to stop the ceremony to receive medical attention. ⁣
⁣ ⁣⁣
Its usually the jigi of a ritual or ceremony that is the most intense, at times days or even weeks...especially with multiple ceremony back to back. ⁣
⁣

At my grandmother's funeral my uncle said to me, "Satan has unleashed his demons to prevent my grandmother's entry into Heaven." ⁣
I will never forget the look he had on his face as he spoke those works. That event replays in my thoughts, fueling my worries if my family knows I am a mudang. Once my aunt yelled at me, you want to be a fortune teller? Those words have a heavy affect when spoken in native tongue - 점쟁이 되고 싶어.⁣
This year, Uncle asked nonchalantly "if people seriously seeks my assistance". I was so taken back by a simple question, but it was my opportunity to take back my power. I responded yes with much enthusiasm, and then he jokingly said 'I dont think so'. ⁣Even my mom who wavers between being supportive and embarrassed. She is worried someone might know I am a mudang. ⁣
⁣
This year, I hope to release those burdens, its quite suffocating. We are taught (colonialism) to demonize and be embarrassed by our ancestors, our roots, ourselves. ⁣Which is why I value and appreciate our rich traditions.

Written by: Kuukuwa Andam⁣
"You are convinced that they are evil & anyone who worships them is wicked. These are the same deities who helped your ancestors live long enough to birth you. Deities who inspired you to keep your environment clean, taught you to have certain rest days from farming & fishing so the land was sustained. Deities who looked like you, bore your names & established your societies causing you to have pride in yourselves. Deities you were terrified of lying to & so swearing before them was more effective than any oath created in a foreign land.⁣
Yet you love deities introduced to you by persons who colonized, enslaved, raped & robbed you. Yes, you admire these deities whose depictions look nothing like you & whose names sound nothing like yours. You trust these deities who have told you they’re currently roasting all your ancestors in hot fire because your ancestors weren’t ‘lucky’ to have anyone tell them about these deities. You also love deities who didn’t care enough about you to ever declare your people as a chosen nation or to write the original versions of their 'sacred book’ in your native tongue So you have to translate it with all its attendant errors & inconveniences.⁣
A century after worshiping this new deity your countries are full of filth, your land is running out of resources, you are plagued with debt & subservient to the very persons who introduced you to these deities & they dictate if you will eat & how much, no one in your country fears to lie, be corrupt or mistreat their neighbor. Now everyone can’t think the same & we should all be free to choose our beliefs or lack thereof. But at least, we can get to the point where we respect the faith of our ancestors, whether we choose to practise it ourselves or not." ⁣

posts.caption:
Ritual ceremony prop called 고 - go. The 'go' comes in various colors, and for each kut ceremony we prepare about 4. ⁣
Different color go are knotted and prepare for use, when the ancestral spirits are summoned. Each ancestor that enters the ritual space and the mudang, grabs a colored go and begins to shake out the knots of the go with ritual music. ⁣
⁣
The go is a very important ritual prop with rich symbolism.  The color of the go is symbolic, an indicator of ancestral han. The spirits that are consumed by their han, uses the black colored go. Its the spirits, that uses the black go...we have to send off properly and respectfully with compassion.  The knots tied on the go, represents the different realms of the underworld. ⁣
Traditionally money is folded into each knot of the go, used as offerings for each guardian of the underworld. ⁣
⁣
During the kut, of the ancestors gori the spirit sometimes tear the go in half, and walks through it as the fabric is ripped along the way. This is very symbolic, because it shows the ancestors is breaking through their own han, and shows the ancestors travelling through the underworld as we guide them to the gates of the spirit realm. ⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣

posts.caption:
Traditions. What does it mean. ⁣
I have been thinking about the many layered meanings of traditions. ⁣
⁣
For me, traditions means ancestors. Its the story of our ancestors and a way to honor our ancestors. Traditions are woven through the stories of our ancestors. Whenever I practice my traditions, its gives me a deeper understanding of my ancestors, their struggles, hardships and joys. As much beauty is seen in traditions, there is also an equal amount of pain, trauma and suffering. In one way, traditions were born from pain -in some form, a response.⁣
⁣
The traditions of the mudang shaman is to heal, resolve and release of the Korean han, of the people and ancestors. Various kut ceremony were created and performed in response to the situation. To simplify the purpose of mudang, is to bring balance and harmony. It also gives me a sense of pride, especially when much of shamanism was brutally attacked, and survived. ⁣A story of resilience.
⁣
Practicing traditions, means understanding and acknowledging the many stories that are woven in it. I believe honoring ancestors means practicing traditions because its a way, a form of reciting their stories. Keeping our ancestors alive in our every day lives, gives a deeper appreciation. ⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣

posts.caption:
Korean Effigy Dolls. ⁣
⁣
Effigy are representation of a person and is present in many traditions. In Korea, spirit tablets in ancestral shrines, or other shrines for housegods and deities are also a form of effigy. ⁣
⁣
These are effigy dolls, their main purpose are for rituals called 대수대명 (Daesu-dae-myung). We collect all the negativity that a specific person is affected by and put it into the doll, performing the ritual providing aid and relief. ⁣
⁣
There are many types of effigy used in the rituals of a Korean shaman -the mudang. Traditional effigy used in the rituals is dried pollack fish. Depending on the severity of affected person, hair and nail clippings are used to dress the effigy, or undergarments of the person. ⁣
⁣
When a person is in their samje cycle of the 3 calamities, many request the 대수대명 ritual to help with the cycles of bad luck. Or when someone is sick, needing a cleansing or an exorcism, this powerful ritual is performed. ⁣
⁣
⁣
We have a very special kut ceremony today - and again, no sleep before a kut ceremony. ⁣
⁣
Todays kut is for an elderly korean halmoni (grandmother). Her story is an incredible journey of sheer willpower, and the hearts devotion she given to her practice. posts.caption:
Absolutely adore and love Korean pine trees. 💕 Each curve and twist of the tree I feel inspiration and honor. When I see a beautiful pine tree, I think of ancestors. Like a great big grandfather or grandmother tree, wise with honor and integrity, and always there. 🙇‍♀️⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
Long ago, there was a giant pine tree and the King with his caravan was travelling until the tree block their path. The King demanded the tree bends to let them pass or else he will come back to tear it down. Just then the branches twisted, turned and parted to allow the King to pass. The tree instead was commemorated as the King's tree. I heard its based a real tree and has been protected as sacred. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
Pine trees is Korea's national tree, its presence is incredibly symbolic.  Pine is also used when a family welcomes a new baby, or its adorned on a casket when someone passes. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
There's even an old Korean village that fitted their home around the tree with their trunks and branches. Imagine having a Korean pine tree just growing out of your livingroom.  I been looking for years if Korean pine trees are legal to plant, because I soon as I can get land - would really like to plant the tree. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
⁣Pine trees are sacred, often used for their cleasing abilities and for their longevity and vitality.  Pine trees also can represent the house gasin spirit Songju (the roof beam god). Along with births and funerals, pine trees are adorned in vases at weddings as the sharp needles keeps evil and negativity out, blessing the space as a protector of humanity, representing the resilient spirit of the people. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
I love Korean pine trees. ⁣❤⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣

posts.caption:
In the kut ceremony various offerings are made to the many gods. Meat offering would either consist of either a pig or a cow. ⁣
⁣
Cows are very sacred to our ancestors, some treated their cows better than their own children.  Cows were sacred because of the help, often cows help plow the fields and used as a workhorse. In older times there were gods and goddess for the cow pen & stable and for the birth of cows. Cows are valuable to Koreans. ⁣
⁣
I read somewhere that pigs were used as offerings more so than the cow because cows were too precious to give up. Also pigs are seen as wealthy and lucky animals. ⁣
⁣
I wonder if that can be one of the reasons why pigs are use for Daegam, the greedy god who oversees wealth, luck and prosperity. ⁣
⁣
Also the type of animal offering is an indicator of the kut ceremony magnitude. If its a huge kut, with clients spending lots of money for the ceremony then a cow is used. If its an average ordinary kut, a pig head or a whole pig is used - especially if it involves asking for more luck and blessings. ⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣

The way I view and think things has always been different than others. Love to look in between the nuisances and diving deeply into my philosophical thoughts.⁣

Look around, everything has been conveniently created to catapult us into instant gratification. Our internet connection now links us faster, Google was used to search for everything, and now we've upgraded to Alexa and other apps. The way our food is created, made and delivered attributing to our fast culture through fast foods and fast fashion of the hottest new trend. ⁣

This also applies to spirituality, many are so eager to arrive at their destination unaware of the journey needed. Traditions are dying. If you ask me, its because our modern conveniences and fast culture has no room or space for 'living in our traditions' or is accepting of them. Korean spirituality has been about your hearts devotion. ⁣
⁣
Traditions are abandoned because its seen as time consuming in our fast paced society. Many are interested in spirits, forming relationships with their ancestors and working with Earth, and being in touch with their roots....without the heavy work or the hearts devotion. ⁣

Today's modern conveniences in our society only attributes to Self, its all about me. While traditions helped connect and realize that its not about me, but WE part of a bigger picture. ⁣
⁣

I hope to one day create a WE, its my life work and mission. ⁣

posts.caption:
My Janggun regalia spirit armor. ⁣⁣
Janggun 장궁 are military generals, leaders and warlords. ⁣⁣
In Korean shamanism, jangguns are very important gods of the pantheon with their main roles as an exorcist. They are gods of war -fighting, expelling and protecting. In the past national military heroes are deified and some mudangs would serve the historic heroic Jangguns in their shrines. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
One of the modern Janggun some Korean mudangs (shamans) have in their shindang (shrine) is American General Douglas MacArthur. Some Korean mudangs believe Douglas MacArthur spirit has deified, and serve as a janggun spirit and part of their pantheon. ⁣⁣He is a Korean hero who saved Korea during the war, and like every great war hero - his lives on, as a Janggun deity for some mudangs. ⁣⁣
Find it quite interesting and fascinating. Douglas MacArthur and his troops helped defend South Korea when forces invaded from the North during the Korean War. Ever since then, Koreans have viewed America as their savior, and began to idolize America forgetting about America's role towards the annexation and occupation of Korea. ⁣America was in favor of Ito Hirobumi conquest, helped spread propaganda that Korea was unfit to rule our own land. ⁣⁣They allied with Japan and desired our country taken away.
⁣
As a mudang, when researching and learning about my folk traditions and beliefs, its hard to ignore the politics and history that has major factor and impact into shaping our shamanism. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
⁣
*Fun fact: night before my initiation...I dreamt of General Douglas MacArthur as a janggun without knowing about his importance. For those curious, no hes not part of my pantheon. ⁣⁣
⁣

posts.caption:
Often asked, why I dont have statues or idols of the gods in my shrine. A shrine can be either called 'shindang' or 'beobdang', a shindang means the hall of the gods, and beobdang means the law, hall of rules -with Buddhist influence.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
For practical reasons is why I dont have statues or idols of my gods - also, I just dont connect with the idol figures. The idol statues are more of a recent representation of the spirits...natural objects , paintings or calligraphy were used. Instead of the statues, I use their tools and items as their symbolic representation. Each tool and item treated and handled with respect as the spirits energy is alive. ⁣⁣
⁣
Every shrine will be different according to each mudang, their lineage, their personal style and their spirits taste. Every shindang (shrine) varies. Personally for myself and my gods, we dont like clutter and perfer to have a more simpler set up. While other mudangs will have stacks of offerings and paraphernalia which suits their style. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣

posts.caption:
Todays 굿 Kut ceremony offerings have been all set in the morning before we gather for breakfast. ⁣
⁣
Especially on a day with a ritual, ceremony or special holiday the spirits - either the gods 신 (shin) or the ancestors 조상 (josang) eats first. ⁣
⁣
In the Korean customs, when gathering at the dinner table or any table to eat....no one lifts their spoon or take a sip of water until the family elder takes their first bite. In my home, we all gathered at the table every meal but did not eat until Grandpa (the elder) or my dad picked his spoon up and took a bite. ⁣
⁣
This is also why, whenever I go grocery shopping I put all the fruits on my altar to offer my gods, ancestors and spirits - the first bite of our food. Eating food thats been blessed by our ancestors is another ritual we call eumbok. Means we receive the blessings of the gods and spirits through the food we offered. ⁣
⁣⁣
Thank you to everyone whose been so understanding,  I had to cancel and reschedule alot of my appointments because of the kut ceremony I was called into. ⁣
⁣
Wishing everyone a wonderful New Year. ⁣ ⁣

In our folk and mythology....
The new moon also accompanied by the eclipse means the fire dogs were released from the dark world. Sent by the lord of darkness to retrieve the Sun and Moon, since no light existed in the dark world. The eclipse shows the fire dog attempting to bite the sun and moon, but failed because the sun was too hot and the moon was too cold. ⁣

posts.caption:
Have a blessed Dong-ji - Winter Solstice. ⁣
⁣
Today was an incredibly hectic day. Cleaning the house in preparation for my mom, staying for the week. Tomorrow we have a kut 굿 ceremony/ritual that took two days of prep work. ⁣
⁣
Today is also Dong-ji (Winter Solstice), I wiped down my altar, cleaned all my offering bowls, cooked red bean porridge as sacrificial offering, laid out all the offerings around our home....with 2 kids at home sick. ⁣
⁣
I unfortunately did not have designated bowls for my shrine, to use as an offering plate. Altar offering bowls, plates and servingware are separate from the bowls/plates of personal use. So I improvised, used clear cups as offering bowls for the red bean porridge. ⁣
⁣
This reminded me that not every offering spread is grand or perfect, especially during older times when food were seasonal. How did mudangs hold ceremonies, ritual rites and other services when supplies werent readily available -they improvised.⁣
In the winters, no fruit grew or was available to use as offering. Instead they made sweet cookies made with honey, dried fruits and nuts using the honey cakes as an alternative. ⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣

posts.caption:
Happy Winter Solstice!⁣
Dongji 동지!⁣
⁣
Its a symbolic day, and the traditional ritual includes cooking patt-juk, red bean porridge.  A small bowl of red bean porridge is served to every room in the house - bedrooms, bathrooms,  closet, foyers, the kitchen, etc. In older times, people would spray the red bean porridge over their doors and windows. ⁣
⁣
The red color from the red bean possesses the ability to ward off evil and expell lowly spirits that may be within the home. Containing yang energy and effective to counter the yin-energy spirits.  Eating ppat-juk is very closely tied and connected to the agarian roots of the Korean culture and recognized as a sacrafical ritual food. ⁣
⁣
The folktale goes a man named Gong-Gong ssi, had a son who died on Dongji and later became the spirit of smallpox disease. He hated red beans and so it was cooked every Dongji to keep him away. ⁣
⁣

My love and connection to the mountains, started since I was a little girl. ⁣
⁣
Growing up, my best childhood memories is camping and hiking. I loved being outdoor in nature I would drag my sleeping bag outside of the tent, while my family slept inside. ⁣
⁣
My favorite book as a kid, written by Jean Craighead George called "My side of the Mountain". Its about a boy who ran away from his town and family, to live in the woods connected to the mountain. He took a dead tree as his shelter, learned how to survive in the mountains.  That is book gave me years of inspirations and daydreams. I enjoy being in nature, I dont mind leaving behind the technology and modern conveniences except for the bathroom. ⁣
⁣
My happiest times is when I am in Korea, sleeping in clay homes with heated floors, climbing mountains before sunrise, praying in temples and shrines -inspiring me, connected to nature, the spirits and the gods. ⁣
⁣
Before all this, I had plans of being a CPA with my own firm while also having a real estate and insurance division. My 16 year old self would not of approved, I was always so serious. For halloween, I dressed up as a business woman. LOL haha. Oh dear. ⁣😬
⁣

posts.caption:
⁣
Birch trees are sacred trees. ⁣⁣
Its the Tree of Life, the Cosmic Tree in Korea, Siberia, Mongolia and various places. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣
👑 In Silla, (present day Gyeonjju) the golden Tree of Life crown  was worn by their kings, queens and head shamans. The crown bears resemblence to the headgears worn by Tungus Siberian shamans. Birch tree has significant importance during the Silla in rituals, the bark was used as a writing tool, and also as medicine.⁣⁣
[Side note: My family clan is from Gyeong-ju]⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Korea founding myth say Tangun was born under a birch tree from a god and a bear woman. The 'tan' signifies the birch tree our Shamanic King was born from by Mt. Baekdu. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Trees were sacred, and were seen as god pillars in Korea.  Mongolians view the trees as 'sacred gateway'. Its said, Koreas connection to the Baikal region Buryats part of the Altaic language is where our Koreas tongue -dialect is rooted from. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣
📷  Photo from our backyard in the Catskills Mountains. ⁣⁣

산삼- Sansam, Korean wild mountain ginseng. ⁣
A herbalist friend gifted us with precious mountain ginseng from Korea. ⁣
⁣
Sansam is believed to be gifts from the gods, a gift from Sanshin. Because this rare medicinal herb is said to harness the energy of the mountain grown by the spirit, untouched by man. When a person finds a wild mountain sansam,  a small ritual of gratitude is performed. Before trekking the mountains to dig Sansam,  a purity ritual was perform by the digger. ⁣
⁣
In one of the myths there is a demonic goblin dongjasam that wanders thr village at night, and during the day turns into plant. One story says a couple decided to eat their son, when they looked inside the pot they realized it was a Sansam and not their son. ⁣
⁣

좋은 초하루 지내세요. 항상 감사한 마음으로 기도합니다.⁣
⁣

I was waiting for midnight to set up my altar and all the offerings but I or my gods, were too impatient to wait. ⁣
I swear, told myself to make the offerings simple..but as I was cooking, different foods kept coming to mind. Next thing I know, I am cooking a feast. 😅⁣
⁣
Tonights offerings are persimmons, giant pomegranates, Korean pears, dried dates, blueberry pie, pear tart, tri color vegetables, fish jeon, crabmeat jeon, sweet potato jeon, rice cales, tofu, cookies, candy, water and liquor. ⁣
⁣
As a family we pay respects to the gods and tutetary spirits that protects and bless us. My sons both bowed and gave gratitude. 💗🙏⁣
⁣
Have a beautiful and blessed new moon everyone.  May your ancestors and guardian spirits guide and protect everyone. ⁣
⁣

⁣
(2/2)Nowdays most mudangs will have to learn all the chants, songs, prayers, hymns and sutras. As well as learning how to use various drums and percussions that is crucial to rituals and ceremonies. The role of 법사 are slowly diminishing due to the highly competitive nature and field of mudangs. Since many mudangs and their training apprentices learn the sutras, most will keep 법사 related work - in house. Paper craft talismans was traditionally handmade for each ritual, has now been taken over by factory mass-produced goods. ⁣
⁣
While there are a handful mudangs practicing outside of Korea, beobsa are mostly concentrated in Korea. Working as a mudang in the US, I've came across only one sutra-reader. Spirit mom, my elder and teacher is a Yeo-beobsa 여법사 (female sutra reader). Although our sutras, prayers and hymns are now written down in form of sutra books. Spirit mom also receives sacred sutras by her gods and often recite prayers and sutras that arent written down and only orally recited. ⁣
Im currently working on preserving her sacred messages and words given through the gods. Songs and chants, that are incredibly unique as she has been exposed to by her grandmother, a powerful mudang who had the ability to heal many people with just a prick of a needle. ⁣
⁣
I have so much training and studying to do, I barely scratched the surface despite the years I been apprenticing. But my spirits has been nudging me to wake up, and 목숨 걸고 (risk ones life, put your life on the line). Indeed this path is bittersweet, often serving as the sacrafice...but I been blessed by the grace of the gods and my ancestors. As spirit mom says, we are the torch that lights the path for many while burning ourselves. ⁣
⁣⁣
••• Spirit grandpa, he is a 법사. I have yet to meet another talent drummer, the kuts are magical with the sounds of his drum. 💗🥁⁣
⁣ ⁣

(1/2) 법사⁣ - The sutra readers of a ritual or ceremony. ⁣⁣
⁣
Often males, and possess multi talents in singing, music and crafts. Their work is focused on aiding the mudangs. In a ceremony or ritual,  the main focus is on the mudang as the ritual center.  The nucleus of the cell, meaning no mudang - no ritual or kut. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
During a ritual or ceremony, 법사 will provide musical support while the mudangs jumps, dances, receiving the gods and spirits directly through trance spirit-possession. ⁣⁣
법사 training are also very intensive, mandatory to memorize the hundreds of different sutras used for space clearing, blessings, exorcism, prayers, chants while having musical gift with the different drums used in a ritual or ceremony. They are also gifted crafters, making paper talismans with sutras, gods and protective deities cut out from sacred paper. While many will dismiss what seems like mere paper craft decorations - unknowingly aware of the magic, energy and presence it commands. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
There many types of beob-sa, some will have strong gods energy 신끼 (shin-ki), afflicted by the spirits sickness, the divine sickness of 신병 (shinbyeong) eventually receive confirmation from other mudangs who says they are "the gods product". Those sutra readers 법사 will most likely receive their 신내림 (gods descent ritual- initiaition). ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
There are also 법사 who may have the spirits energy but not enough to become a mudang. These 법사 provide musical talent during the ritual and ceremonies. But still some will force their way into initiation, hoping it will bring them better luck, prosperity and life. Most 법사 will develop working business relationships, a partnership. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣

I connected with @shaman.mudang this weekend and had my little mind blown by the flood of knowledge with which Mudang Jenn graced me.⁣
⁣
Since getting into minjung theology and learning some of the histories of western missionaries’ work to depoliticize Korean Christians during the Japanese occupation of our land, I learned that in our desperate desire for survival, we lost ourselves. We were taught not only by the Japanese imperialists but also by the white missionaries who are fearful of anything unfamiliar to them, to see in our reflections, faces of uncivilized, uneducated, demonic savages. What hurts is that we believed it. To this day, Korean Christians demonize our past and those who carry on the traditions — *our* traditions — that have carried our ancestors and their survival for more than ten thousand years. ⁣
When I met with Mudang Jenn to talk about Korean shamanism, I did not expect the depth of passion and wealth of information. She is a kind heart with a brilliant mind that is continuously accusing more knowledge. Hearing her talk about our people’s history, I felt overwhelmed with appreciation, love, and reverence for the generations and generations of Korean women who rose before their households and the sun to traverse the woods of the mountains to pray in the dark and gather fresh water. If you are Korean, I urge you to follow @shaman.mudang. I am so grateful that within our diaspora community, we have a mudang, our kin, with such an abundance of cultural memory.⁣
⁣
▪︎▪︎▪︎⁣
I feel extremely blessed to met and encountered such a passionate individual. Extremely honored that there are many interested in the stories and life experiences of a diaspora mudang. ⁣
⁣
Much gratitude and blessings to you and your ancestors for connecting us and sharing their messages and wisdom. ⁣
💜🙏💙🙏💗

⁣
I was on the phone with my spirit sister Mia @yellabear8 , we were chatting about a client who did a kut ceremony. The conversation wasn't serious, and all I said was the clients name.... Christine (Chinese and Laotian)⁣ ⁣
Then, in the corner of my room, stood a woman dressed in red with gold embellishments and gold threading. It took a moment for me to fully understand what was going on. ⁣
⁣
I wasnt sure if I was sensing and "seeing" correctly.⁣
I had to abruptly interrupt our conversation. ⁣
⁣
Instead I brought my focus to the lady standing in the corner of my room -dressed all in red. With short hair and glasses, short and incredibly overweight. She wears a scowl as her natural state, many wrinkles, pale white skin with a hairy mustache and giant mole on her face. ⁣
I was rattling off to mia all the feelings and messages I felt bursting out of me through thoughts, feelings, sounds and sensations. I felt insane with a smudge of self-doubt. ⁣
⁣
But it was the most vivid and visual experience I ever had of a person's ancestors. Alot of the messages didnt make sense to me but regardless of what I blabbed, Mia wrote it down. Super thankful for...because I have the worse memory (foggy memory). ⁣
⁣
Received validation that I wasnt losing my mind, Christine said I described her mom exactly. ✊😎😅⁣
Even when it seems our ancestors arent listening,  somehow and in some way Christine mom still managed to pass on messages that brought closure, guidance and future oracles. ⁣
⁣
In the picture,  I have rice in an offering bowl that is set for Bulsa Halmoni.
⁣

posts.caption:
The DMZ. ⁣
North Korea has been in my thoughts. My families both originated from before the regime, before the war. People freely travelled up and down the peninsula. ⁣⁣
My biggest regret. Not hearing or knowing about the stories of my grandparents, of my ancestors. All my elders have departed  this world and now finding their peace in paradise which we call 극락세계 (geukrak-sege). ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
I hope and wish one day, that I can step over these chained-link fences and barbwires. ⁣
When my ancestors walked through this land, they ran for their lives - terrorized. When I walk through this land, I hope - dignified. Its the sacrafice of my grandparents, and their parents that I am standing and breathing today. Its the very reason why I am free and others are not. Its a sacrafice that I (luckily) will never have to make because of the life privilege and luxuries I have been given. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
My grandmother left everything and everyone. Arrived alone. No family. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Settling down in Paju, a maeul (village) located outside the DMZ. I imagine grandma settled there in hopes one day the barbwires comes down...she can run back to find her family. ⁣⁣
Grandma passed away when I was 16, I was too young and unaware. I hope maybe in my lifetime I can help fulfill my ancestors wishes. ⁣⁣
We are part of the cycle...⁣⁣
Once we were the fruits hanging on our ancestors trees, to eventually grow fruits of our own...becoming their future ancestors. We receive to give back. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣•••••••••••••

People often forget "comfort woman" included women from China, Philippines and other occupied countries. ⁣⁣

When I was in my early 20s, living in a posh neighborhood of Astoria, Queens. I would never forget the train ride I had that day. A homeless man entered and everyone scrambled,  some even cursing at the person. I was so enraged, how is  anger or disgust the first instinct when clearly this man was struggling for food and shelter. ⁣
Despite my anger and disgust at the situation...I was disappointed in myself. I struggled, if I should speak out or say something. Instead I feared and worried at the possible backlash, and kept my mouth shut despite my fustrations. ⁣
⁣
Here are some stats. ⁣
In September 2019, there were 62,391 homeless people, including 14,962 homeless families with 22,083 homeless children, sleeping each night in the New York City municipal shelter system. Families make up more than two-thirds of the homeless shelter population.⁣
⁣
Families. Children. Your community. Our community. ⁣
⁣
I'm not rich, anyone who comes into my humble home and sacred space can easily see that. But I hope to teach my boys humility and compassion. ⁣
Because....everyone in some way or form struggling to be accepted and notice. Not invisible but visible to their community. ⁣
⁣
We will be putting together care packages of emergency blankets and socks to dustribute this cold weather. Please DM or message me if you would like to help or contribute in donations (even a $1) to help us make these care packages. ⁣ ⁣⁣

posts.caption:
A shipment of specially handmade incense just arrived from @zishutraders.⁣
⁣
"Dakpa Tamdin Incense is a traditional Tibetan incense and a Tibetan family owned company based in Nepal.  This incense is pure and hand made, manufactured in accordance with centuries’ old traditional Tibetan formulations and under experienced supervision. The incense recipes were taught to the family by Tertons and Rinpoches who use this incense in their own rituals and on their shrines. It contains traditional Tibetan medicinal herbs and precious substances.  This incense is formulated for religious purposes, meditation, and relaxation." ⁣
⁣
Ribo Sangtsoe means “Mountain Smoke Offering”. This incense can be used to cleanse and purify the mind of impurities, misgivings, stress, and to be filled with spiritual satisfaction and happiness for this life and the next.  Along with prayers and meditation, it is also used while hoisting prayer flags.⁣
⁣
Minling Surpoe (Black) contains ingredients used in the old sacred incense of a Nyingmapa monastery in Tibet alled Mindrolling. It helps create peace of mind in the person using it. This is mainly used for Kyilkhors (Mandalas) as it contains all of the substances and herbs, permitted in Kyilkhors.⁣
⁣
Shingkham Kuenkhyap (Yellow)⁣
Shingkham means “World of the Buddha”, Kuen means “everywhere” and Khyap means “spread.” This incense contains all the requisite herbs and substances required for the rituals to worship and please Gyalwa Rignga’s Shingkham. By offering this incense, we get the blessing of worshipping the Buddhas.⁣
⁣
Sambara (Orange)-⁣
This incense was among the first kinds to be produced in Tibet. It contains all basic herbal ingredients which have been used in Tibet for centuries.  In the Buddhist scriptures, “Dho Tharpa”, it is mentioned that Gyajin (Indra) offered the aroma  Dukpoe to the Buddha himself. From this early document, we learn of the importance of Incense in Buddhism.⁣
⁣
Cant wait to use these special incense in my practice, and give my support to the artist. ✊💗⁣
⁣

These socks were special because in older times moms and grandmas would spend their nights mending socks by candlelight. ⁣

posts.caption:
Whats your SAJU 사주? ⁣ ⁣
In older times, when asking for a person's birth information, we would say "give me your saju". ⁣
Saju refers to the 4 pillars that breaks down the birth information. Saju, the divination method of reading a person chart with elemental influences.⁣
⁣
When the 4 pillars of your birth date and time is analysed and broken down into elements into 8 characters, we call that Saju Pal-ja 사주팔자. Each person chart showing the distribution of elements, living with his/hers/their unblanced misfortunes and life destiny. It reveals relationships with those around you like parents, children,  siblings, etc. ⁣
⁣
Korean folk traditions and customs are also about family relationships more so than individuality. In a marriage ceremony, especially for Korean customs it isnt about the individuals getting married but more about 2 families joining as one under  the Heavens. ⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣

[Post 2/2] Trigger Warning ⁣
Domestic Violence ⁣
⁣
Then later, I walked out and left my other relationship after many years. There was dishonesty, but also the feeling of low-self worth. He wasnt physically abusive with his hands, but his words stung like blades. Constant verbal assault, making me feel inferior and insignificant to the world. He would sit down, and ask me what is it I do, that's so good and pick apart everything about me. If he was late to a meeting because he overslept, he would kick me out of the house early morning. ⁣
⁣
I realize despite my vow to myself of not repeating my parents abusive cycle.  I was here creating my own, making excuses and accepting this life. ⁣
⁣
Abuse was the only thing constant in my life. Abused by my own family...my cousin "Gloria" would give use corporal punishment like holding a heavy wooden chair over my head for hours. At night she would send my cousin Peter and siblings into the room, while she held a knife to my throat. Or hit our backs with a metal mop pole because we failed to hold wooden chairs over our head for hours. ⁣
⁣
I've had many incidents of sexual assault by my trusted friends, and others including my brothers Tae Kwon Do teacher. ⁣
Despite abuse being a constant factor in my life, I rised above my situation. I finally put my foot down because I refuse to be held down. I learned to find my voice, strength and courage to finally stand up for ME. ⁣
As a mother of 2 young boys, I teach them humility, respect and compassion. ⁣
At times, the trauma of my abuse can hinder me especially towards my husband. When I forget he is on my side, supporting all the many parts of me. ⁣
⁣If you are in an abusive relationship or setting, it's not your fault. We dont control the actions of others, but are in control of our thoughts, feelings and action. ⁣
One good friend taught me, "Living well is the best revenge" and I intend fully to live well in my mission, and path or kiss my mudang ass.
⁣

As a child growing up, I watch my mother get hit by my father daily. One night, I think my mother finally had the courage to ask for a divorce. Angel and I sat on a bench to talk, but out of nowhere his fist landed punches on me. As he broke my glasses, my spirit and dignity. Gae-cheon known as the "Opening of Heaven" refers to 3 October 2457 BCE, the date when Hwanung (환웅) descended from heaven. ⁣
Chamseongdan stone altar is said to be built by Danggun (founder of Korea) himself. This altar is set up on the peak of Mani Mountain, used to give sacrafices to the Heavens for over 4000 years. ⁣
⁣
In the past, all the Kings of Ancient Korea has all come here to give sacrafices to the Heavens, here at the Chamseongdan Altar.  Ceremonial sacrifices and rituals were held here till Joseon period. Even now, Koreans still give offerings to the Heavens and Danggun. ⁣

posts.caption:
Sam-saek Namul 삼색 나물.
⁣
The tri-colored vegetable, a direct result of the Buddhist influence since the Three Kindom Era along with the ban of meat. With the Mongol invasion and the ban was lifted, meat offerings were used for rituals like jesa (ancesreal rites) ⁣
⁣
The three vegetable represents root, stem and leaf, and the colors white, green and brown. All coming together to emody prosperity. ⁣
⁣
The white root of the bellflower respresents our ancestors, the root and foundation of any family. The brown stems of the fern braken represents the support of our parents (the present). Lastly, the green leafs represents the future of the family. ⁣
⁣
Many ask me, when they set their offering tables if it is mandatory to have all dishes? Can I just have rice and fritters, or just rice cakes?⁣
There are times when I just have fruit or just rice cakes. But then again, I do my full offering in my shrine monthly and small offerings -daily. ⁣
⁣
I can't tell you what you should do, because our traditions and customs clearly speaks for itself. Setting an offering spread requires you to spend money, and for those who have a hard time financially - its difficult. If you can only afford some fruits only, I am positive your spirit will be touched by the offerings, although small but speaks in volumes about your respect and dedication. ⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣

⁣
When we go to Korea for our pilgrimage, spirit mom strictly abides by that. She won't wake us from sleep, she just gets up and goes regardless, if we followed after or not. After much thought, I understood the deep lesson and values that she was silently teaching me. Spirit mom always led by example, she always shown me through her actions. ⁣ ⁣
She has taught me what I do in my path, and the type of mudang I want to be depends on my dedication. In the  winter nights, she would go outside to pray as the snow accumulated on and around her. She always taught me to never break prayer even for a sip of water. ⁣
⁣

posts.caption:
Moon Rabbit ⁣
With the mid-autumn festival , it reminded me of the Legend of the Moon Rabbit or Jade Rabbit. The moon during the Chiseok is believed to be the brightest and fullest, symbolizing abundance and prosperty. The Moon Rabbit (Jade Rabbit) lives on the moon, pounding a huge mortar with rice to make rice cakes. ⁣
⁣
Legend goes the Emperor of Heaven decided to test the faith and loyalty of the rabbit, fox and monkey. Emperor disguised as a beggar asked the fox, monkey and rabbit to bring food to eat. ⁣
Monkey returned with fruit, fox returned with fish but the rabbit was only able to bring grass. Feeling ashamed, the rabbit lit the grass on fire, jumped into it sacraficing itself. Touched by such sacrafice, the emperor placed the Rabbit on the moon to become the guardian. ⁣
Modern day story includes two rabbit, people thought the one rabbit was too lonely and sent a friend. Two rabbits making rice cakes under a cinnamon tree symbolizes the coming together of family. ⁣

posts.caption:
Photo from Google Steemit. 
Chuseok has a meaning of 'Autumn evening with a bright moon'. Its a holiday for ancestral memorial services and the tending to ancestral graves. Day starts with preparing an offering table with steamed rice and seasonal foods. Offerings must include (토란국) toran-guk, taro soup. (송편) songpyeon called pine needle rice cakes shaped half moon rice cakes with filling.⁣
⁣
Its also a holiday that signals to the farmers that it was time to relax and enjoy fruits of their labor.  Korean farmers tried to predict harvest based in the moon's shape, color hue through moon divination called (달점) dal jeom. Red moon sinaled signs of drought and white foretold lots of rain, interpretation varied from region and farmers. ⁣
⁣
I will be setting my altar tomorrow with all the traditional offerings. Happy Chuseok⁣ 💖🙏📿⁣
⁣

⁣

We had an impromptu discussion about our roots, and why they still go out to perform. ⁣
This particular Pungmul (farmer dance group) has been established for 40 years. The director told me her background is in dance and traditional arts. ⁣

posts.caption:
Dad, brought a box of Korean grapes for the kids and family. But before we can open, wash and devour it... it must be offered up in my shrine. ⁣
While the gesture may not seem like much, but it's a huge act of respect. The spirits eat before me, they are taken care of before me. A mudang should ONLY look to her gods, and those shaman with strong gods, their gods would expect that much. It's the reason why mudangs left their families, their parents and children, starting anew. Why? ⁣
A shaman is a vessel, a living embodiment of the gods but not every shaman is the same as their abilities varies. ⁣
Think of it like this...mudangs are conductor of the spirit world, just like copper's great conductors for electricity. Not all conductors are the same despite their qualifications.  I don't know what type of conductor I will be. ⁣
⁣
When making water offerings, those with traditional bowls will come with a lid. Offering bowls must never have a lid on or closed.  The lid should be placed to the left of the bowl, and all altar items should be washed weekly, which is a ritual itself. Same thing for your incense, its should be placed to the right of your incense pot. These are the little details that are often overlooked but necessary in creating proper foundations of our work. Everything is intentional and mindful, awareness must be present at all times. Not something that is easy for myself either, as I am still learning despite the few years already.⁣
I may have the marks of the gods, the necessary ingredients to make me a Mudang. But that doesnt mean, or guarantee me success as one. It's all about how deep our relationship with our gods are. ⁣
⁣
⁣

Homemade 막걸리 makgeolli 🍶 ⁣
⁣
The light sparkling rice wine is the oldest agrarian spirit beverage in Korea. The tradition of makgeolli goes back to the ancient Three Kingdom Era and predates soju. Known as the peasant wine, the 'farmers  liquor' it was the drink of the farmers, the working class. ⁣
Makgeolli is also a traditional offering that is used in every ceremony and rituals. It's used in giving offering to the land, the house gods, wandering homeless spirits and many other ritual, rites and ceremonies. ⁣
⁣
Modern Ritual for Car⁣ 🚙
If your car has been in the shop for repairs or maintenance. We give pour a little bit of makgeolli or any liquor on each wheel - to give as offering and blessing. ⁣
Just like when our homes undergo any renovation and construction, the spirit of the home and land is disturbed. While a 고사 gosa ritual is performed for a home or a business spirits., we pour liquor on the car wheels. ⁣

posts.caption:
The offering table and spread for the ancestors. ⁣
I took the picture from this perspective to show, why we set the offerings in this way.  When we are facing the table, we are facing the ancestors. From our view, the first offerings is fruit but turn it around. Then from the ancestors POV, it's the last row. ⁣
The structure of setting an offering table is very practical. The first row of offerings would be their rice, with water and soup. Next row, is their side dishes (banchan) to enjoy with their rice. Then comes the liquor, with rice cakes, cookies, candy, sweets and fruit - the dessert round 'so to speak'. ⁣
Customarily, we would put money on the rice cakes to ask for blessings and luck. Money was also put on the candy plate for the children spirits of the family. ⁣
⁣
When we speak about ancestors, we refer to blood ancestry and those who we have fated destinies (인연) with, like in adoption and step parents. ⁣⁣Of course, having more family means more work for us. 😅⁣ 🙏
⁣

posts.caption:
Regularly starting to stir awake at 5am, the first task I set out to do is wash up. I must be clean hygienically before I step into my shrine room for prayers. ⁣Just like I would tidy and clean up my altar daily....I do the same for my body which serves as an altar for my gods.
⁣
Going into prayers, in the darkness of the early morning reminds me of the family matriarch sacrafices. It was OUR mother's and grandmother's who would trek out into the mountains at 3am in straw shoes, to pray to the gods for their protection and blessings.⁣
⁣
Our matriarchs would sacrafice their time, lives and bodies to show their dedication to the gods, through bows of respect and worship. It was the women who had the natural ability to dedicate their life, sacrafice their life to the gods/spirits for the well being of the family. ⁣ ⁣
Prior to converting into Catholicism, my paternal grandmother held many mountain worship rites and rituals alongside with Mudangs. She was tenacious, and a woman of pure strength and unwavering dedication. Although my grandmother wasnt the nicest person to me. I admired GREATLY the dedication, the HOURSSS of daily prayers she did for the betterment of our family. A sacrafice she made that was unnoticed and underappreciated. Growing up whenever grandma went into prayers, we saw it as a nuisance and an embarrassment. Looking at her life now, must of been lonely and what a huge commitment and sacrifices she made for our family. ⁣
Now that it's my turn to uphold my family AND the community, serving as a mudang. My home, life and time is dedicated to my tribe and community. When I rise in the early mornings, I do my bows and prayers like the matriarchs before me....I can finally understand, the struggle, sacrafice and dedication. ⁣
Those straw shoes they wore to trek the mountains, the bows they sacrafice over their bodies.....has become my shoes, my path and 'rock to polish'. ⁣
⁣

posts.caption:
Eopsin, god of stored wealth (household fortune). ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
2 winters ago, in the front of my home I spotted a snake blocking my path.  A few months later, another snake appeared. It was such an odd occurence to have a snake in front of home not only once but twice - in NYC, in winter. ⁣⁣
I notified my spiritmom, she instructed me to move out of the house asap. I was upset, and did not listen. I wanted to stay for a few years. Little did I know, the signifance and the meaning of those events for me. ⁣⁣
Eopsin 업신 is a gasin 가신, a house deity that protects the home and the family's financial possessions. The sacred ways in which eopsin is emobodied varied, and included danji (earthen pot), straw bundles, animals like snake, weasel, toad, mice, etc. The most common is a black serpent, or a snake. ⁣⁣
⁣
When a sepent is seen leaving the permieters of a home, its a fortelling sign of family's decline, money loss, and  winds of unfavorable events. Some viewed the snake as ancestral spirits leaving, that you've lost their favor and protection. 조상이 더는다. Either way, snakes leaving your home is an inauspicious sign. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Things got much noisier within my family, alot more headaches and lost money. We experienced so much bad luck, even scammed by our landlord and by my client. We did move out of that home, and now in a better home.⁣
⁣
▪︎NOTE: this does NOT apply to everyone. I'm being flooded with messages about the shamanic meaning of snakes. ⁣I have altars and offerings set monthly to my house gods and deities. This would make perfect sense for my situation, and what I do. It would be difficult to apply it to others. ⁣⁣
⁣

⁣The korean shaman culture, many ways to perform an exorcism. Red pepper flakes are important, as we believe color RED and spicy wards off spirits. Since spirits are of yin energy,  and spicy is of yang, it's used to ward off.

posts.caption:
Today being called to my local area for a 고사 GOSA of the home. ⁣
⁣
Our culture and traditions are based on animist views, we believe in spirits of every type. We had tutetary spirits of a home as well known as Gasin 가신. ⁣
⁣
Whenever a home has undergone renovation or any type of construction, its customary that a GOSA blessing ritual is done. ⁣
It's because the very nature of construction is destructive to the environment around us. But also disturbs the local land deities, as well as the tutetary spirits of a home. During construction,  since the spirits dwelling might be disturbed, the gosa will help put back all the spirits and energies back into their rightful place. ⁣
⁣
When erecting a Korean traditional home Hanok, when the roof structure and beams are in place, a GOSA is performed. Because we believe that Korean homes are alive and the house roof beam deity will come and become a tutetary deity that protects the home.⁣
⁣
What are some of the tutetary spirits of the home? ⁣
We have a bathroom deity who is known to despise children, and is enemies with our kitchen deity. So no food in the bathroom. [Maybe this is where my bathroom fear comes from😑] We have door deities, inner quarter deities, pantry deity, and so on. ⁣
⁣
In our traditions, our home is alive and shared with humans and tutetary deities. ⁣ ⁣ ⁣
(Picture of my offerings to my door god, using window ledge as an altar)⁣

posts.caption:
⁣Today I'm heading to Williamsburg, Brooklyn. ⁣⁣ ⁣⁣⁣
⁣
FYI, I was pregnant here in this picture ('13)⁣ ⁣
My spirit family and I was called to perform a 고사 (go-sa) ritual to cleanse the land, appease to the local deities, and bring in the winds of abundance, luck and prosperity. Asking the gods to their aid, to bring in good cleansing protective winds. ⁣
For a new business opening to serve the Williamsburg community. ⁣ ⁣
⁣
•What is a GOSA 고사?⁣⁣
It is a blessings ritual, for either a home, new business, construction sites and especially for movie production and premieres. A gosa traditionally can be performed by anyone, setting up an offering table asking the local spirits to bless rather than cause any blockages or mischief. ⁣⁣
Mudangs (shamans) are commission for gosa because nowadays most dont know the proper etiquette to perform such a traditional ritual. Also commissioning  a mudang to perform a gosa is different than a gosa ritual performed by a layperson. The chances of success of a proper gosa in my opinion, is better. ⁣⁣
The mudang has the ability to invoke the gods of her personal pantheon and of the local land. To call the spirits to her through song, dance, music and chants. ⁣⁣
The way we perform the gosa is a small ritual kut in itself, as the Daegam (God of fortune) must be invoked and traced possession by the mudang. Daegam grace and bless us with a promise to help with succession when the offering stands erected on a trident spear over a bowl of sea salt.⁣⁣
Salt acts as a purifying or cleansing agent, to protect and purify the offering to Daegam. ⁣⁣

posts.caption:
Early morning hike up in the mountains. 🙏⁣
⁣
We rised early in the morning, the beautiful scenery of fog kissed mountaintops. We saw the sun rise.  Drove through the dewy mist along the curves of mother nature. ⁣
Have a great beautiful morning. ⁣
I wish I can build a house right alongside the life source of our precious Sanshin (god of the mountain) ⁣
This year I am sad that I wont able to go with my spirit family for their yearly pilgrimage to Korea. It's one of the things I look forward to the most. 😟⁣
⁣
Its definitely not a vacation of leisurely activities. It's hard work , travelling day and night to visit all of the sacred shrines and sanctuaries. Sleep is a luxury, and we wake every 2 hours to pray, sing, chant under the moon in the mountains. After a 4-6 weeks of traveling, my body is physically exhausted while my spiritual energy feels explosive with vibrancy. ⁣
When I think about our ancestors, I'm so inspired by their tenacious will. Climbing mountains with straw shoes, performing hundreds of bows in honor and gratitude to our gods. Our ancestors were amazing, their sacrifices and dedication I am truly inspired by. ⁣
I hope when I meet my spirits in the other realm, I hope that I can greet them with integrity. Pat me on the back, telling me that I did well, bringing them honor and respect. ⁣
⁣
What more possibly can I want? ⁣
It's my life's work. ⁣
Dare I say, it's my legacy. ⁣
⁣
⁣

posts.caption:
Morning meditation by the river, in the mountains. Just what my spirits and gods wanted. ⁣
I sat on a rock, and watched the river waters rush around me. I untied my hair, washing it in the river -just like my ancestors did. Letting the waters carry away my dirt, negative emotions and energy. Leaving me renewed, refreshed and grounded. ⁣
⁣
My sanctuary is the mountains with their cold rivers running through. I can sit here all day and night, hypnotize by their lulling tones. ⁣
Part of me doesnt want to go back home, I just want to sit here. Completely emerged a d engulfed within the songs of nature. ⁣
⁣
⁣⁣
⁣
Did you know? ⁣
Traditionally when before an initiation, there has been counts when the spirit mother (elder) would make the initiate bathe, in the ice cold rivers at night. Regardless of the weather or season. The initiate was put through difficult taks and test, to determine their test of  strength, endurance and character. ⁣
⁣

Relations between South Korea and Japan have been combustible ever since Japan colonized the Korean Peninsula from 1910 to 1945.⁣⁣
The diplomacy between the two nations began to sour when the Korean Supreme Court ordered two Japanese companies to compensate the wartime workers. A ruling that Tokyo said violated international law and believe was settled by theTreaty of 1965. ⁣⁣
⁣
Their methods and tactics on political policies, trade and agreements rings in the same tone when Japan forcibly annexed Korea in 1910 before the Occupation. Japan still to this day, argues they were legal and justified. ⁣ Their actions to some, feels like continuously pouring salt over our wounds.⁣
⁣⁣
⁣Everytime we have a kut, the ancestors enter. We released them from the chains of their han 한 and suffering, setting them free. I hope the restless spirits find their peace and resolve, helping restore balance in the 'Land of the Morning Calm'. ⁣
⁣
I hope the two nations can work towards resolving the generational trauma and ancestral pain. The journey towards peace and healing starts with open dialogue. ⁣⁣
⁣
