Tobacco isnt a traditional offering that we [mudangs] give to our gods, but interestingly, I have a traditional smoking pipe resting on my altar for my gods.  So I laid the offering next to my spirits pipe, as I went into my night prayers.

I also have to plan my own ceremony,  called a magi kut. After my initial initiation,  it is proper to have a ceremony year after year, paying my respects and gratitude for my spirits. Also the magi kut ceremony allows the gods to enter and leave. Last year I had my ceremony in March, a few months after the birth of my 2nd son. As  a 'baby' mudang of sorts, I did not expect any new gods and deities to enter. Catching me off guard especially when I had 3 more spirits last year. This year if I can find the time to do it right before the new lunar new year enters. I wonder if any spirits will enter or leave. 
Clients have now asked for their own candle, and since I did not have the proper ceremonial bowls. I went out in middle of the night to purchase temporary ones until  I place an order in Korea. Each candle is written with the name and birth information, and is placed within a bowl of rice. I do my bows and prayer daily, and those who have a candle are always included in. It seems my altar will soon run out of space, and may have to get something custom built for those candles. My altar is currently 10 ft long and 4.5 feet wide, if I can...get a even bigger space.

I wish I can live on top of this mountain for its view and for the immense sacred 'ki' that flows. It feels that I am literally in the heavenly world among my gods and deities. 
This view is more breathtaking than the picture itself, stirs and moves something within me. The waters of my heart flowing as I take everything in. 
I understand why the many ancient kings of Korea has taken the journey to this mountain's summit to perform ancient rites and rituals to the heavens. Being in the same place where so many prayers and offerings is given, this entire place flows with vibrance and energy.  The base of this altar is circular to signify thr heavens and the top part of the altar is shaped square to signify the earth. This is where the heavens meets the Earth, and who can argue with that. This sacred place still holds its value and meaning when mudangs [shaman] hold ceremonial rites on Koreas founding day. 
I been thinking of going back next year (2019) to join hands with a knowledgeable professor about all the deep ancient shamanic meanings of our mountains, a way for diasporas to learn of our roots and the stories of our gods/deities. If anyone is interested in touring with me please let me know. 🤗

Yongwang, our Dragon King was very specific in his message for me. He echoed the same message as the other gods in my other vision. He spoke of the rainbow orb, and what I must do to maintain it.

My dear Dragon King has bestowed upon the greatest gift, he allowed me to see and reconnect with my grandparents. To carry my gods, and ancestors I must be the living vessel, such an honor I have been given. I am even more grateful because once again, they breathed new life into me, saving me.

용왕님 said 'Do you see the color of my oceans, how the fish and other creatures can thrive in my waters'. He explain the work he does to provide, the polishing of one's rock. He told me your body is a temple, a living temple. Your ancestors,  spirits and the gods all follow you and live within the waters of your heart and soul. It is up to you to keep those waters clean and pure.

.

posts.caption:
We made our way to the next destination,  to the underwater tomb of the Great Munmu Daewang. Our beloved Dragon King of the sea. 
We rented a table alongside the beach, that would give us shelter from the winds. There, other mudangs were scattered across the beach, all drumming and praying with their offerings. 
Even Buddhist monks were there with their own clients, hitting their moktaks. Praying to the Dragon King in a ceremony/ritual where they purchase back a fish, and release it into the waters. 
Amazing sight it was to see monks and mudangs side by side. Other monks rented rooms that looks like a small 신당 "sindang'. Through the window, I can see that he was jumping up and down, while banging on his cymbals. At first I was extremely fascinated, and then I became upset. The Buddhist has their culture, their traditions and ways rooted from India. But why is it that these monks, steal from the Mudangs? Our ceremonies, dance and songs through imitation? 
Ive had plenty of clients who came to me for readings, wanted to find out the reason and source for their unhappiness and life misfortunes. When they walk into my "sindang" 신당, I see their spirits and ancestors. I tell the clients that they have to send away the spirits that pesters them. Most of them tell me that they did such ceremonies with the monks at temples. This is dangerous, because their methods has no effect on the godly world of spirits, ancestors and gods. Why is it so many are against Mudangs? We are demonized but then everyone imitates us? We live in a world full of patriarchal dominance, and Mudangs are [mostly] females holding the power, that must be scary to the men.

comments.text: As an Indian, allow me to clarify. Buddhism does not enjoy the same popularity in India that it does in East Asia and other parts of Asia. Ironic, but true. India, in the very pagan sense, developed to a lifestyle/religion we now call Hinduism. However,  East Asian Buddhism fascinates me
However, East Asian Buddhism fascinates me
Sorry for the double post***

However, East Asian Buddhism fascinates me because there is very little by way of the original teachings as people shape things to their own way to adopt something new. The Buddha was obviously born a Hindu and Buddhism largely is derived from Hinduism. This being said, India and Hinduism itself is extremely diverse and it is almost impossible to know all the cultural systems that exist. posts.caption:
In a small tight alleyway stands two stone Jangseung, a stone totem pole. The guardian of the Korean people and their villages. 
You couldn't tell at the entrance of the alleyway is one of the MOST expensive space - the Myeongdong shopping district. I hated walking through this district with all the Korean beauty stores. The dense crowds of people moving in masses to shop for same thing - makeup. Ugh.
When I walked by and saw these guardian deities, at first my heart sang with joy to find something I can connect to. But soon felt somber, as I realize they have been forgotten. Just shoved aside like some decorative figure, with its people unable to realize the significance and importance. I came to Korea to reconnect with my roots, walk a sacred pilgrimage to pay my respects to my spirits and ancestors. Instead this trip taught me more, and instill a burning fire within me to protect the sacred traditions that are being destroyed and forgotten. 
A long time ago, someone use to constantly asked me, what good will you give to this world. What can you offer? He tore at my core despite his intentions....instead it made me push harder.

Even in my teen and early adult life, abuse was an ongoing theme. My grandmother was so obsessive with her faith that it blinded her. She became the wedge that divided me from my father. As she planted seeds of hate into his mind. She called me names like the devils child, satan and child of a whore all because she did not like my mother. I grew older and began to have relationships which would later echo the same abuse whether it was physicallyor mentally. Those relationship always went longer than it needed to, despite the abuse. I been in many circumstances of rape, and sexual abuse of adult men and male friends or colleagues.

The values and characteristics that those around me failed miserably at of integrity,  respect and honor are my GREATEST assets.

posts.caption:
(Part 1 of 2)
Most people are curious who I am, how did I end up on my path. Questions about me, as a human and as a person. So for those to get to know a little more about me. 
Born and raised in NYC, lived all my life here. Both parents immigrated from Seoul, Korea in the early 80s. I'm the eldest of three. 
I did not come from a complete family, in fact my early childhood and home life is quite dysfunctional and broken. My parents divorced at the age of 9, and my mother walked out of our lives due to the intense abusive situation with my father. He was an alcoholic and a domestic abuser. We moved from place to place, under the care of my grandmother and our aunts from my father side. He worked hard all day and night running a 24 hour small grocery store to provide for the family. 
Growing up was certainly not easy due to the abusive nature of all my family.  My cousin who was in charge of us, gave us corporal punishment of holding chairs above our heads for hours while on our knees. Sometimes she would make us plank while beating down on our backs with rods and sticks. She had a lot of trauma of her own, but the adults in our life left her unchecked. Aware of the abuse but turned the other cheek. 
My family was strict Catholic,  an intense type of Catholic that is not normally followed by the Church.  My grandmother held her own rosary prayers at night, and station of the cross which I was forced to attend and endure. Every weekend we drive to LI, and pray at the outdoor shrine of the "Shrine of our Lady". We always went at midnight, despite weather conditions. Rain and snow did not stop us, just meant we had to layer more. I use to look at the stars in the sky and wonder if heaven knew my pain. 
I went from a bright bubbly child to a shy, timid person afraid to speak and show my personality. School was the worse, I went to a Catholic school called Queen of Peace. Which didn't help me either due to the severe bullying and teacher picking on me. 
Continued in the next post.

posts.caption:
The "falls of the 9 Generals" known as Gujanggun 구장군. 
Spirit mom told me of a dream she had many years ago. She came to a place of double waterfalls, and while she sat in prayer. A mighty Janggun (장군) approached her, and said Ah, there you are. She said in her dreams she was so scared that she almost fell into the waters. 
Two days later after the dreams, in the silence of midnight she and my other spirit sister walked their way through a forest path. Came across these double waterfalls by chance, and she realized it was the one in her dreams. Immediately she set up an altar with all her offerings that they carried. They sat there frozen to the ground since winter had arrived. And just like her dream, she almost fell into the ice cold waters. 
There is an ancient legend with these falls, that 9 Generals gathered here at the waters. They formed a pact, a truce and commitment to go into battle with their lives. Those generals went to war with pride and honor, and won their battle. 
A special place she wanted to share, of the mighty 9 Generals of Korea. 
I sat there in solitude, engulfed by its beauty and peace. I began to sing my mantras, and went into prayers. Again the waters of my heart began to stir, as I was overwhelmed by emotions of the significance of this place.

Can you feel the pain and trauma of this place. Do you see the pagoda in front of you, the 5 tiered stone granite pagoda. 
This pagoda was assumed to be built back in 1316, by a monk when the temple was being refurbished. 
The roof of the 2nd tier, 3rd tier, and the 4th contains bullet holes made during the Korean war (1950-1953). The original temple was built by Doseon a master who systematized Feng Shui theories in 887. Unfortunately the original temple was destroyed in the fire of during the Imjin war, the Japanese invasion of 1592. All of its buildings burned down except for this stone pagoda. 
In 1959, is when monks started to rebuild. .

Part (2/2) 
A soft glow of light walked towards us. I couldn't see through my tears until she was standing right in front of me. Her hair was was twisted in double loops, I call it '토끼 머리' means rabbit hair. Her garment was so seamless looked like flowing waters. 
She took the black lump from the Jangun hands, and covered it with her own. She began to glow as she seemed to put her energy into the black ball. She put her hands in front of me, and slowly uncovered the ball. It was no longer black, instead looked like a orb full of intense bright colors of the rainbow.
I did not know what it meant at the time, as no words were spoken only gestures. She seemed very pleased as she showed joy in the ball. She gave the colored orb back to 장군 Jangun. He took the orb, and pierced my heart again with his sword. He placed it back. 
No words were spoken but the visions spoke a thousand words. The message was clear, I knew I was given a gift. It ignited a colorful passion within me, the energy of the gods was alive in my heart and body. I felt renewed, reawakened. 
We packed our bags and belongings, but my tears were still flowing. Spirit mom told me to walk around the mountain path, to let the 기 energy flow in my heart. My group left me behind to give me privacy,  and instead I sobbed my way down.
It wasn't until in the early sunrise, did I see the shrine. My heart was literally going to burst, as I came across the shrine for the Heaven Maiden 선녀 Seonyo. I lit a candle and incense,  I began to bow and pray because of the overwhelming gratitude that was pouring out of me. This was an affirmation that what I saw was right, especially to see the shrine for 선녀 after my vision. I made a vow right then and there, to refortify and renew my promise to my spirits and path. I hope to light my path with blazing colors bringing hope and healing.

posts.caption:
Super excited to hear about many huge projects in the works. A lot of opportunities are coming that will allow me to share my lineage, culture and the musok traditions that so many diaspora are trying to reconnect to.
Every lineage is different, as every mudang and gods have their own personality.  There is a lot of "gray" areas in the musok/mugyo tradition due to much being passed down orally. 
But yet, there are basic core concepts of our work that serves as the backbone, core building blocks. 
Not many knows, but there are obviously many types of mudang. Being initiated does not guarantee a title of a mudang. "볼려 먹어" basically it means if an initiate has the ability to call and use the gods. Those who can't 볼려 먹어,  usually just have a small space for the 단지 (danji) which usually a pot or bowl that serves as a mini altar for their spirits. These people can't really be called a mudang or shaman because they don't have the ability to call or use their gods. Instead they serve the spirits through prayers and ancestral veneration. 
Usually when people hear they have spirits,  automatically they assume initiation that is untrue. There many ways for people to respect and uphold their spirits and gods without heeding the call. I've seen a lot of things most people would not believe and I am super lucky to learn from the best amazing mudangs of all, my spirit mother.  I always tell her, that I would be happy if I can be just an 1/8 of what she is.

Night prayers at a mighty mountain known for its feminine energy, yeo-san-shin 여산신 the female mountain god of Ilwolsan. Named after its shamanic nature worship, the mountain means sun-moon. This place has shrines set up for San-shin, seonyeo, jangun, and many others. 
We climbed up the mountain and set up our offerings and prayed under the moon and stars of the night. 
And we are up this beautiful morning at 4am to prepare for another round of prayers. Setting up offerings, and praying to our gods. 
Next door, at the Sansin shrine another mudang came and set up for a kut ceremony. They banged their drums and gongs. In 2 hours they finished their kut ceremony, I asked spirit mom how can they finish a ceremony that short? She said some mudang schedule kut ceremony 3 or 5 in a day. She said that is why us, mudangs have a bad reputation because money is first for others.  She said we can never do a ceremony in that fashion, it would be improper. 
Back then a luck/blessings and ancestral kut ceremony took 3 days....minimum and its disheartening that the very sacred traditions of our way is twisted by the hands of the mudang who are the keyholder.

posts.caption:
I've arrived in Gangwon-do 강원도 after praying at Seoraksan 설악산 and Odaesan 오대산. 
Tomorrow, I will be making offerings and praying to the Dragon King of the East sea. Afterwards I will be right by the DMZ (Koreas Demilitarized Zone) that separates North Korea from South Korea. Spirit mom is granting my request to stop by the zone so I can finally pay my respects. 
Although I can't enter, I will make prayers and small offerings table. My ancestors came from North Korea before the war. My maternal grandmother was the only one in her family who made her journey safely before settling down in 파주 Paju. Grandmother never spoke of her past, family or any trauma that she endured. Instead she kept on living and she kept on going, despite the hardships. She became a refugee of sorts during the war, and had to resettle. 
Paternal grandpa came from the North too, and as the war broke out grandpa was forced to join the military and fight for the Japanese side during WWII. He even spoke of another family he had, when he lived in Japan while serving the military.  He had a wife and child, and when the war was over. Again, he was forced out of Japan and separated from his family. He was never able to establish contact,  and passed away in 2012. 
I wanted to go, so I can pay respects to the gods and most importantly pay homage to my ancestors. I know they have been waiting for me. 📿

posts.caption:
The ancient altar of Dangun known as 'Chamseongdan' located at Manisan 마니산. Manisan has been a site for shamanic worship since ancient times. Some shamans consider this a 'demon expelling' mountain and this very mountain to have the strongest 'Ki' energy of Korea. 
This altar is said to have been built by Dangun himself. Dangun the founder of Korea (2333 BC) offered sacrifices and ritual ceremonies to the heavens here. This site is believed to be over 4000 years old, underwent a few renovations but still maintain its original form and shape. The tradition of offering sacrifices continued on with the 3 Ancient Kingdoms of Silla, Baekji and Goguryeo kings even up to the Joseon period. 
Ceremonies are still held here yearly.
This site also houses the Korean hornbeam tree regarded as the oldest and most beautiful of its species, designated as a cultural asset in '09.
Based on the legend, Dangun ruled as king for over 1500 years. At the age of 1908 years old,  he retreated into the mountains and became immortal Sanshin the god of mountain.  It is said this mountain represents heaven,  and I couldn't agree more. 
I sat here  in silent prayers despite the screaming winds, thought I might literally be blown away. This mountain feels as if I am standing at the entrance of heaven with the gods.

posts.caption:
•Do you see the crow perched on top of the tree? 🐦
Birds are seen as messengers of the gods, between heaven and earth and many birds are considered sacred like the magpie, ducks, cranes and etc. 
On my way up the difficult trail of Manisan 마니산, I reached a point when I seriously contemplated if I should continue climbing up to its summit or if I should call it quits. my legs trembled as it carry me up the mountain side. 
While sitting and feeling defeated a crow just happen to be above my head in a tree. It squawked as if it called to me, to get my attention. I thought to myself if it was the spirits (as a joke) but just then it started to laugh at me. 'ka-ka-ka-ka' as if taunting me on my defeat. 
Did not think anything of it, until the bird flew to my right side and perched on the handrail. It cawed and squawk again but the sound was different. 'Hana-dul, hana-dul, hana-dul' it screamed. 
At that very moment I wanted to collapse from emotions because my grandfather used to say that. He would say 'hana deul, hana dul' as he always walked because his legs didn't work well. "Hana" is korean for number 1. "Dul" is the Korean number for 2. 
the crow flew in front of me still cawing 'Hana-dul, hana-dul. 
Took a picture to remember this moment.  I picked myself up. 'hana-dul, hana dul'
I counted as I silently cried my way up to its peak.

Part (2/3). At the foot of the Guksa-dang we made our offering to the Jangun (general warlord). Spirit mom laid candles and incense, with offerings and she sprayed soju over us to perform an exorcism to cleanse and purify. 
As moved up along the shamanic  shrine complex, we came along various altars and shrines to different god's. Yongwangnim (Dragon king, god of the sea) shrine is where we set up the bulk of our offerings, we sat down on the cold stone floors and began to bow.

Then we made our way up even further to the Seon-bawi. Spirit mom, lit another incense and candles. Spirit mom began her chants and shaman songs, I could no longer hold back. The quietness of the shrine was soon filled with my cries, as I pound my chest with my fists.

posts.caption:
(Part 1/3)  4am prayers at Seon-bawi #선바위, the main sacred point of Mt. Inwangsan in Seoul.  It's noted that even Korea's past Kings came here to pray and meditate. 
Seon-bawi or Gijaam is one the world's most worshipped rock, the primary reason why it's considered one of the holiest mountain. Below the Seon-bawi or Gijaam lays the Guksa-dang #국사당 - the National Shaman Spirit shrine, therefore enhancing and enforcing the sacredness. 
This rock natural formation is call Gijaam because in the past married woman came here to pray for child-bearing. Or others say, the rock looks like a monk wearing robes, and is called meditation rock. Some say the rock resembles King Taejo founding King of Joseon along with his Queen or his close friend Master Monk Muhak. 
Others say, they see the rocks as the great monks sitting in contemplation and protection of Seoul city. And some maintain the 'original' ancient views with a mystical twist of male/female Buddha's to help relieve sufferings. 
Historically, when King Taejo founded Joseon his friend Master Monk Muhak wanted to include Seon-bawi within the city walls, but royal advisor and leading Neo-confucianist 'Sambong'  advocate to exclude them, symbolically excluding Korea's native indigenous shaman culture. 
At the mountain peak sits a natural rock figure which is said to be the Benevolent King himself or Sansin (Mountain god). Next to him is a rock figure of his tiger (guardian) and a dark magpie stone figure perched behind.

posts.caption:
This is my most precious set of hanbok (한복), this was worn on my last day of initiation (3rd day). The day I "married" my spirits and received my heavenly mandate
An initiate must always have 2 (two) sets of new hanbok for their initiation. One is worn during the first two intense days of initiation, and last clean new set is worn when the mudang receive their mandate. 
One set has a yellow top/red dress bottom, and the other has a green top, red dress bottom. The colors of the hanbok is crucial and hold lots of meaning. Yellow jeogori top 저고리 with red chima bottom 치마 are the colors of unmarried girls. Green jeogori top with a red chima bottom are the colors of marriage. We (mudangs) are getting "married" to our gods 신, when we get intiated. That's why I wore this set on last day of initiation, it's my wedding hanbok of sorts. It's the core basics, etiquette and respect. The foundations which we lay on is important! 
White is color of death, mourning and underwear. I have seen initiates wear color white hanbok on their initiation day. It's like saying your initiation is your death, you went to meet your gods in sheer undergarments or you are in mourning, in our traditions. Usually after that, we are free to wear other types and styles of hanbok when working in a ceremony. 
How many sets should I get made.

Those who abuse their power and spirits will later become chained and imprisoned, not knowing it. Created their own demise, and the sin they commit becomes a strike against your spirits/gods tainting their light. I too made many mistakes, and learn from those gravely because they come back to you over and over. 
It was March, just a mere 6 months passed after my initiation in Korea. I was a newborn, didnt know much. One day someone reached out for a reading, one of my first online reading. Took us 3 hours, with lots of tears, crying and stories. We connected and then 1 month later, her entire family flew over to me. For a week and half, we prayed in the mountains and the oceans, and then we initiated her for 3 long hard days. 
She was older than me, could of been my mother. Her health was on a decline, with heart isssues and lungs that burned, we worried how will she get through 3 days of initiation. The first day of kut, she flew....
We were amazed how someone so sick could manage such hard strenuous jumps. As she jumped, tears filled my eyes because I knew the reason. The same bittersweet pain was staked in my heart, not a dry eye in the temple. Everyone gathered to support our new sister, but we all cried sharing her pain, we all mourned together.

posts.caption:
Sotdae 솟대. 
Birds are seen as messengers of the spirits in the Korean shamanistic traditions. Its is assumed that the sotdae is deprived from connection of the 'Cosmic Tree' and 'Sky Birds'. Sotdae are spirit poles like totem but different. Long poles out of either wood or stone, with a bird figure on top. The significance of the poles is prevalent in North Asian shamanism and related to the world-axis whic connects the heavens to the earth. 
The bird figures were never carved, instead kept original wood shape, only de-barked to show natural beauty. Many bird types of sotdae were found like geese, magpie or crows but ducks were mostly used. Ducks were given important meanings due their ability on land, water, and air was thought they they can control rain, survive floods and protect villages from fires. Ducks were also part of Koreas founding myth.
Originally placed at the village entrance along with the Jangseun (totem) to wish for peace and good harvest. 
During the Joseon period, sotdae symbolized when a scholar passed a government entrance exam for celebration. A sotdae facing South to wish for good weather for farming,  facing North meant to bring rain.

Today is new moon offerings. Yesterday was Columbus day or Indigenous People's Day.
Honoring our ancestors and natural spirits was a normal way of life. The man in the picture has set an offering table to the local town guardian. These town guardian known as jangseung (장슨) are wooden totem poles of Korea. Located at the entrance of the village,  to ward off evil and protect the villagers within. Jangseung were worshipped as gods, often the town held ceremonial rites to give thanks to the guardian deity. 
Jangseung, the Korean totem pole has also been found on roads to provide companionship and protection to the travellers. They are made to resemble the villagers, a symbol of their ability to stand tall despite many difficulties. 
Happy belated Indigenous Day.

We met up early in the morning, drive out with our trunks full of supplies. As we set up, thats when we realized the sheer horror of forgetting to pickup ricecakes (dduk) 떡. 😫 Spirit dad and I, drove back out to Flushing to pick up ricecake order, and drove back to BK.

posts.caption:
Part 3•
Lucy's dad took his time to enjoy the ceremony, he and the other ancestors spirits all calls it "janchi" 잔치 which means 'party'. Back then, kut ceremony were treated like a neighborhood block party, held outside in the yard of a persons home. Everyone in the village would be invited, you will eat foods only available at a "janchi" or special occasion. 
Lucy's dad walked over to me, and gave me a few words. Told me that I made the best decision in accepting my path as a mudang. I chuckled because spirit mother tells me the same. He told me, there was nothing else I was allowed to do but this, and only this. That is very bittersweet. 
Lucy dad was having a good time that he forgot about his wife. Lucy's mom was waiting on the other side. 🤣 He asked to bring in the Kiasengs so we can dance and play. We told him to party with the kiasengs on the other side, and quickly but gently sent him on his journey to the spirit world. 
I hope maybe one day, I can hold a kut ceremony outdoors. All walks of life invited to share food, drinks, laughter,  a sense of community and leaving with full tummy and hearts. 
A lot of people are called to something, whatever your passion is. It just so happens mine is my spirits, my gods and working with them to help others.  Being a mudang [shaman] is NOT important, my title or what I am is not relevant. But...how I walk my path as a mudang IS important. It's my bones, my core integrity is what sets me apart from others. The very basics, the foundations of how we treat our gods, our spirits and ancestors can say a lot about a mudang's bones. (Pictured is the helmet of my generals/warlord god)

•Part 2. 
Lucy's dad was the last ancestor left, spirit mom grabbed his hanbok and we started the drums again. He entered her, and she began to sing.
First thing he asked her, he really wanted a drink, that his daughter poured. She bowed and poured him a drink, he was happy. He said he felt so good, the 잔치 벌린게 (party/ceremony) he was having a good time. He asked Lucy, remember when you were in school and I braided your hair crooked. Lucy screamed and she cried, she said that was her fondest memory of her father as a child. She laughed and giggled through her tears, as she told us how much her father hairstyles were so bad 'country bumpkin-like' that she was always teased. She said she didn't care, felt like she was the luckiest girl in the world because her dad did her hair. 
Lucy dad, was quite a personality. He loves to sing and dance, he was smiling so much that it began to stir the emotions of my own heart. The sisters all looked at me puzzled because it was such a happy occasion. Instead I had tears streaming down my face. The music stopped and everyone asked why the sad face, why the tears. 
I told him, thank you. Watching him (Lucy's dad) sing and dance brought me to my knees. I was so grateful that we was able to 'peel off the layers' and now that he has fully healed from his own trauma. I don't know why, but that moved me so much. To see them, shed away their pain and sorrows. Transform it, heal from it, move past it and blossom into a beautiful spirit spreading his love, joys and laughter. What's more beautiful than that.

posts.caption:
I am constantly learning more about my shaman culture, and often includes the politics and history.

When Japan first took over Korea, it is said that the Japanese recognize the spirits (Heavenly) of and the Ki (energy). They determined that to break the strong spirits, Koreans must receive their energy from our mountain. (One of Koreas most important shamanic god is Sansin, god of mountain)
The Japanese hired Shamans and feng shui masters to map out vital points of where the energy or spirit of Sansin is alive. They strategically drove iron stakes into the mountain, purpose of it is to kill the spirits. 
After Japan lost, Korea set off a new program promoting hiking to it's people. Asking it's people to climb the mountain to search for those iron stakes and rods that were driven into the mountains.  So that's how Korea became a country that it's people love to hike. 
To this day, there are some hikers that still carry on the mission of restoring order and the spirits back to Korea.
History is important. •
I am now even more upset as my friends in Tibet just informed me that Korean Christian missionaries went to Tibet and drove stakes inscribed with Bible verses into their mountain. I find that disgusting and disgraceful, upset at their actions.

Happy Autumn Equinox! 
Happy Korean Thanksgiving known as Chuseok, which literally means Autumn eve. 
A major holiday in Korea with its customs tracking back to the Three Kingdom era. It is said this ancient custom was taken from shamanistic rituals that was held on the Harvest Full Moon. 
A custom that respects our elders and ancestors. Traditionally an offering table is set for the ancestors known as charye. And the sacred pilgrimage to the gravesite of your ancestors is still practiced today is known as seongmyu. 
May your spirits and ancestors look favorable on you and your loved ones on this beautiful Autumn Equinox. 🤗

posts.caption:
Sleep has been evading me in the recent weeks. 
An important kut ritual ceremony is upcoming in 2 weeks. A renewal ceremony with the intentions to block, samje 삼재 the 3 years of bad luck.
When the ritual ceremony date is chosen, things will start to happen. The ancestor spirits of the client will start to visit, either to tell you their story or for acknowledgement that they are there, waiting for the ceremony. Dreams may be more vivid and active, my days will be affected by their influences. 
While we were talking,  a young boy popped up...told me he was hungry.  I saw an image of him, in very raggy cloth monk attire that was too small on him. The sleeves of his arms came half way, the length of his pants were mid ankles. He was a dark tanned child with a bowl haircut, he also had an underbite. He made notions of a head injury, but most importantly he made sure that I knew he was hungry. The 'chigi/jigi' which is like empathetic spidey sense I got, is hunger and being cold - which meant he wanted clothes. A ritual ceremony was already place, so it meant that he wanted to be included, meaning we had to 'grab' him during the ritual. 
I later found out it was her older cousin from Korea. The reason why he had cloth monk clothes was because her family owned a Buddhist temple. He passed when he was a child due to prolonged head trauma from daily abuse. She forgotten about him and cried, she told me it was very sad....that he appeared to remind her not to forget him this time around. Her cousin needed to release his 한, the traumas of his life. And so, I will pay extra attention and care to him on ritual day. Make sure he is full from his offerings  with new clothes to wear...on his journey to the Spirit world guided by his guardians. Trauma free, pain free...just free. 🙏

My spirit mother. My rock, the torch that ignited my soul.

She is the reason why I really strive to walk in my path with integrity and honor. I know she put her hopes and dreams into me, our lineage, legacy and fate. That itself shakes my heart to its core because no one supports and believes in me, more than her. 
Walking this path, I've shed alot of tears...with her wisdom, shes shown me more compassion in this world. She always taught deeper lesson that are unseen to the eye, taught me absolute true sacrifice. She has shown me through her actions and her work, what it really means to serve our gods/deities and people. 
I've met many shamans and teachers, but the minute I met her, I just knew she was the one I been looking for. I will never forget my first moments/interaction with her.  The minute I found her, the minute I stepped foot in her temple...I collapsed, and uncontrollably tears kept pouring. I was so grateful, still am incredibly grateful for her. 
One of the most important lessons I learned from her is what my role is...the true lesson and meaning. Why do we light a candle when we pray? She said our roles as a shaman, is to provide light to the world, but in order to light the world we must burn. The ultimate sacrifice...she continues to live by this, as I now do, taught by her. Every prayer, every ceremony,  for any client I will 목숨을 바쳐 (give my life) and do my work.
My family, my children means the most to me. Its for them, I do what I must do. Most people think its a choice, as simple as walking away - its not. But that is not my reality or saju (4 pillars of destiny), the service I am called to, shakes my very being. I worry that I may not be bright of a light to this world, I worry that I am undeserving of the gifts my gods gave, and undeserving of the many blessings I was given. 
I will forever walk my path in this physical world and the spirits world trying to repay the gratitude that is overpouring in my heart.

posts.caption:
Temple care is essential and crucial to korean shamans known as mudang/manshin/bosal.
My spirits and gods, required me to have a full temple and altar without fully knowing how much work, dedication and obstacles there is. What it means to serve our gods fully, be the caretaker of our ancestors. Not everybody is capable of handling the duties and responsibilities of a temple.
We must pour water into the same bowl, while eventually it becomes a robotic chore. There are lessons in our mundane tasks.
In the beginning I used to just pour the water, just to pour as a sign of respect. But over time I learned that when I pour water into their bowls, it's not just pouring them water. It is the intentions that I have, the Gratitude and gratefulness that I have when I give my offerings.
A lot of my students tend to look beyond the horizons not realizing the crucial building blocks they are missing to develop the relationship with their spirit, gods and ancestors. Relationships are not born overnight and it applies to a shaman. After being initiated.... there is no way, you are able to differentiate between your gods and spirit. It feels like a giant ball of Play-Doh mixed in with colors, and as you develop your relationships you will begin to understand and differentiate.
The spirits chooses the shamans, but that does not mean our destiny comes to us with no sweat, tears or work involved.

posts.caption:
Happy 칠성날 (Chil-seong day)
Chil-seong is the Korean shamanic Heavenly deity/gods of longevity specifically for the wellbeing of children. It also literally means 7 stars, referencing the 7 brightest star of the Great Bear constellation also known as the Big Dipper.
Although Chil-seong is depicted as 7 individual but treated as one deity. Chil-seong the shamanic deity later absorbed into Buddhism, Taoism, etc. Because Chil-seong is very prominent, it is easier to find them at a Buddhist temple than other shamanic gods/deities.
Today is a day of Chil-seong (칠성), usually any  family with children would visit the mudang, ask to be included in the Chil-seong ceremony. Each child name is written on a long piece of white cloth to represent their life line. We put up offerings, we drum and pray for those children. Ask for the heavenly Chil-seong god to hear our prayers, our songs. That each child whom we pray for grows big, healthy and strong. 
칠성 Chil-seong is one of the oldest worship god/deity in the Korean shamanism.

To protect the families and their children the names have been blurred out

posts.caption:
As promised, Mudang or Musok Monday. 
Someone asked if a shaman is the same as a fortune teller and vice versa. 
No, not everyone can do both. 🌸Some mudang shaman can do fortune/jeom (점) reading, but cannot peform in a kut ceremony. 🌸Or some shamans can do kut (굿) ceremonies but can't do any fortune 점 jeom reading.
🌸And there are mudang shaman who can do BOTH fortune 점 and 굿 ceremonies. .
Why?
Not every Mudang Shaman serve the same gods, every pantheon is different. There are also many different levels/tiers within the positions of the gods. So not every god may be the same. Every Shaman gifts varies as it all depends on the pantheon. Some shaman are just born with innate abilities while other must diligently work hard polishing their rock to develop it.
For example, just like a pizza slice 🍕 from NY is NOT the same as a pizza in Texas. They are both pizza, but one is better than other. It's kinda of the same thing, while there are a lot of mudangs or shamans....everyone's gifts varies. 💬What distinguishes a shaman from a fortune teller?
Well, a shaman is someone who had a  properly initiation kut 굿 ceremony and a fortune teller comes in many forms. With the popularity of new agers like tarot, reiki astrology, etc. It's inspired alot of people to get in touch with the spirituality but now everyone is learning these things. Just like there are many astrologers or tarot reader, you can learn through classes and books. Not saying anyone can learn to be a shaman but it's different. 
For example, an organic vs gmo 🍅 tomato. one was naturally born to be a tomato, while other was created. 
Oh dear hope my examples makes sense and not confused you even more.

An initiation ceremony is an intense process. It's literally a fight between life and death, to the mudang. Before initiation, the shaman to be is at the mercy of the spirits, and it's not glitters and rainbows. It's agonizing torture, suffering, it feels like my soul was slowly suffocating.
The mudang and other indigenous shamans that I know, never went this path willingly. If anything, we fought the calling of the spirits for most of our lives until we were barely hanging by a thread. So when someone comes to me and say please initiate me. WHY?! What intentions do you harbor that you desire to be initiated? What false misinformation did you read online that made you think, this was for you. 
Some have this fantasy misguided thought, that once initiated they will have almighty magical powers. 
Umm No. 
This isn't the X-Men. 
After initiation, you will learn to pour water in the same cup over and over. It's called being humble and learning humility. Ever see karate kid, yeah he didn't learn those Flying Kicks on first day of class. 
So when someone approached me asking to be initiated, I usually a raise my eyebrow asking Why? This path is difficult, and involves rock polishing, walking in a path of mindfulness. No one is ready for this

Most get upset that there isn't much one can do on their own with the spirits like other spiritual paths. Like what?...

Guys, there is a reason why I say to establish a relationship with a properly trained and initiated mudang shaman. This isn't some thing you can wave your smudge stick and meditate away. It's a reason why people are chosen are marked by the spirits, why they are called and not you. If you are interested in learning more about Mugyo, or any spiritual paths of other indigenous traditions do it under the proper guidance.
I will happily and seriously spend my time helping anyone with their questions about this path or their life. You don't have to be Korean to get a reading to glimpse and see our ways, our views and reasonings.

Many Korean diasporas reach out to me about reconnecting back to their ancestral roots. Most are interested in learning about the ancestral traditions of our culture, our indigenous shamanic practice & beliefs that dates back to prehistory.
Roots. Our roots are important. 
A flower plant cannot survive without their roots, it's through the roots they are able to grow. If the roots of that plant become diseased, then slowly the plant itself becomes diseased as well. 
Ancestral veneration (worship) is important and to honor them would be a kut 굿 ceremony. Through this ancestral kut ceremony, can we treat those with diseased roots. And since those roots are hidden away underneath the dirt, unseen to the plant. In the ceremony, we open the doors of the spirits, inviting them in to tell us their story, their joys/pains. Its the spirits with the most pain/anger known as 'han' (한) that need to heal from their traumas of this world. The cold will be clothed, the hungry will be fed and drinks given to the thristy. Yesterday's ceremony was one of the most heartbreaking, its a story of a solider who fled when the Korean war broke and how his family suffered because of his actions.

posts.caption:
Those who are chosen/marked by the spirits assume that once initiated as a mudang, your sufferings ends. I answer that yes/no. 
Yes the suffering you endured (shinbyeong, shaman sickness, spirit sickness) or whatever other names its called, that stops. The ancestral sickness you had because of your ancestors spirits at your side, that too, stops.
I geniunely feel for those who are suffering, living a life that feels like a curse, those who cant make sense of what is and isnt, etc. But because of our sufferings, it is what gives us the ability to connect with those whose soul may be suffering silently. 
I had it hard. In school I use to get bullied, I was shy, quiet and weird. Weird because I use to talk about demons, ghosts and spirits. Hated school bathrooms. Hated dark hallways. Went to alot psychics only to be told it was a family curse. Dreams started to become vivid, almost screaming at me. Sleep paralysis episodes was so frequent it made me terrified of the night. Visions happen impairing me briefly for that moment, I was scared shit.
But despite all that and more, I grew from it. I learned compassion and empathy at a young age. It doesn't matter if your saju says you are mudang shaman, or that you are talented/gifted all the fields of our work. You got to put the effort, polish your rock, walk in a path that aligns with your soul and spirits. 
Suffering is the magical main ingredient to what makes a great mudang shaman. Its beautifully bittersweet. We are also misunderstood, but it comes with the path.

posts.caption:
This week's kut ceremony has me all sorts of messed up. I didn't know how ungrounded I was until the night before the ceremony, I sat down to pray/meditate. As soon as my eyes closed, immediately a young man appeared and he did not look good...he looked ill, disturbed, in grief. He did not give off a good positive vibe.
I quickly jumped up and ran to my kitchen to prep ingredients for a cleansing quick mini ritual. I had to send the spirit of that weird young man away, restore balance within my home. A small part of me was also doubtful of myself but I have experienced this way too many times to just brush it off.
As soon my ingredient were ready, made my exorcism/cleansing concoction I throughly went around my house, and then exited out of my front door. There, the battle just begins. I throw my knives down in attempt to cast out the negativity through my body with my general warrior gods. The knives land favorably, but I cast my knives again to make sure that energy had left. I finish and complete my mini cleansing ritual with the ripping of the five color fabric.
Next morning, I was brushing my teeth and somehow began to choke. But it didn't make any sense, how or why I was choking. I felt my throat was cut off and I couldn't breathe, felt myself turn blue and heard my partner call my name out of concern. I felt my eyes roll back and then somehow it just stopped. I quickly gathered my spirit tools and headed to the ceremony kut site. I asked my spirit mom about the ancestor spirit of the client whom we are doing a ceremony for. I asked her if among the ancestors, is there a young man who passed away...in a violent way. She told me that there is an ancestor spirit, the clients older brother passed away young from suicide by hanging. I felt a chill, and I knew I should never doubt what my gods tell me. I'm even more nervous about my future to come, I know I have big shoes to fill with my spirit mother legacy.

My temple pantheon currently occupies the biggest room of my house. Its a gesture of respect to my gods/deities. 
In Korea, most mudangs have small shrine/temple cramped rooms. Its also because Korean provides convenience because the mudang's home shrine temple does not need to occupy a big space. They need just enough space to take clients for readings. If a kut ceremony is needed, they go to a 'kutland' 굿당 and there like a spiritual resort, they provide all your kut ceremony needs including cooking, cleaning and lodging. 
Here, mudangs in America we dont have those luxury of renting a venue for our ceremonial needs. Instead we do everything in house, so we need to make sure our  temple room has ample amount of space for the ceremony. 
Although my temple occupies the biggest space in my house, its still not enough to do a kut ceremony comfortably. 
One day I plan on building a temple nearby the mountains and hopefully provide a 'kutland'. At least for my spirit family usuage.

posts.caption:
Over in the far corner is the offering table of the Daegam (대감) god. 
Its a very important part of a kut ceremony especially when the ceremony is to make someone better. Its a diesase/sickness kut ceremony called byeong kut (병굿). Having his separate table with his offerings is needed for a special ceremony such as this. 
He is among one of the first gods I connected with. I will never ever forget that moment when I was moved by so much emotions when his part of the ceremony came. I didnt know who he was at the time, but he always touched my heart. He is forever my Daegam. 
Encyclopedia of Korean Folk belief says 'Daegam is universally portrayed as a greedy character that brings with him material fortunes, and also as a two-sided deity that brings to people both material gain and troubles. In other words, Daegam expects humans to pay attention to him and offer devotion, and if this expectation is not met, the deity brings calamities and causes pain for the family.'

posts.caption:
Daesin god descended and she opened the spirit door for the ancestors to enter. I was eagerly anticipating this part of the ceremony, to reconnect with my maternal grandparents. Instead the first person to enter was my paternal grandfather and he scolded me. "You are a descendant of MY family lineage not theirs" (referring to my maternal lineage). He yelled at me that I look down upon him and my other ancestors. As he was walking out, he said he will return. My spirit mom sends my grandfather spirit out by walking out through the back door. There by the back door typically, the JeoSeung Saja 저승사자 aka Korean grim reaper awaits to escort the spirit back but when my spirit mom re-entered the room....the door reopened behind her. This happened a few more times during the the ceremony...
In my Magi 맞이굿 kut ceremony I did not expect to have my gods play musical chairs on me and switch things up. I was taken back, I felt their energy, their power and their desires.
She told me to think of the magi kut as an another initiation ceremony. Towards the evening, the bottom of my feet blistered up and peeled. The energy I felt channeling through me was so aggressively intense that by the night's end I was bruised everywhere. 
But I couldn't stop, I pushed myself harder and harder to jump. Each god entered and left, made their presence known. I poured my heart and soul into everything in that ceremony, I gave up everything. 
My amazing teacher and spirit mother asked a group of us..."why do we (mudangs) light candles when we pray, what is the meaning of it". She explained that our role as a Mudang/Manshin  is sacrifice, giving myself to my gods. So candle symbolizes that, sacrifice ourselves for the good of others, to help.

posts.caption:
There different types of shaman...
And there are different types of mudang. 
My spiritual lineage is of the heavenly celestial gods, than having a lineage line rooted in the earth bound spirits. 
The difference between mudangs whose spiritual lineage is rooted by celestial gods vs earth gods is the energy type. Also the way we finish our initiation differs... Mudangs with celestial lineage will "ride a pot filled with clean water", that earthen pot signifies the dragon god and we (mudang) neeed to strive to become as clear and clean as the water which we ride. 
Other initiation requires the dancing on top of the butcher knives. While both is a sign that the mudang has received her title/authority from the spirits...they are different. 
Mudangs with lineage in the Earth bound gods tend to be more aggressive, confrontational, demeanor is sassy, smoking, drinking, cursing and behavior isnt so refined. While I need to be more conscious of my actions...polish my rock, carry the burdens of my family and spirits, need to be better, self sacrifice. Responsibility are the same, type of work we do are the same....but there is a small difference
The work we do is the same, we perform ceremonies and invoke our gods to help those who seek the help of gods whether its related to health/sickness, luck/fortune, ancestors relief, love/marriage, etc.

posts.caption:
Happy Lunar New Year aka Korean New Year. 
We call this day 설날 Seollal. 
The first day of the Korean lunar calendar. It is one of the most significant holiday, celebration lasting 3 days.
Earliest record of this celebration was in the 3rd century. 
Its an important day to return to your hometown, prepare an offering table to past ancestors. The ancestor offering ritual is called charye or jesa. 
When family visits their elders, we perform Sebae 세배. Its worshipping of your family elder, a ritual act of respect and filal piety. Sebae involve the act of bowing to pay our respect to the elders. Usually you perform one bow to your living elders and three bows to deceased ancestors. 
Children would receive money from the elders, and carry them in silk pouches while dressed in traditional korean clothing called hanbok. 
Along with the traditional offerings of fruit, rice cake, liquor, water, vegetable, tofu, fish, meat. Its a special day to eat rice cake soup called tteukgook. Its made of white rice cake signifying purity and cleanliness. 
My children gods ask me for money, so I put some under their shoe in their altar and then put it in their silk pouches. 
Happy New Year 🤗
새해복 많이 받으세요
Means receive many luck in the new year.

Its an important milestone celebrated in the korean culture. Long ago babies didn't survive past infancy due to lack of medicine and proper care. Babies that live up to 100 days meant that they will survive to see their first birthday. 
It is said when you share rice cakes with 100 people, the child will live a long and healthy life. Thats why its said you shouldn't eat Baek-il rice cakes alone.

posts.caption:
People are usually divided in regards to anything spiritual. Are mediums/psychic/shamans real, fakes or frauds? 
The one question I absolutely f***king hate is, how come you dont know lottery numbers. Or asking me to "predict" some petty BS like its a circus freak show. 
Let me ask you, do you expect an oncologists to know when he/she will get cancer. Why not? Its their specialty, their field, shouldn't they know when they will have cancer? If not, must be a fraud and a not so very good doctor. 
Or how about someone who is employed at the lottery, shouldn't they know what numbers are going to pick the lottery winner? 
I will never claim to be 100%, because there is no such damn thing.  Can a doctor cure every person that walks into their office, NOPE. 
I have had very few clients who I didn't connect with, to me...that just means that our destiny/fate path didn't cross. But when I do connect, which is the majority of my clients...its a beautiful thing. 
Just like you cannot dictate or force living people to do something, same thing with the spirits. While you may have a burning question, dying to know the answer...but the spirits has other plans and wont answer, bypassing your question. 
Just because I see, sense and communicate doesnt mean I can force a spirit to anything. Im not a spirit slave driver, just someone who senses them. 
I use to doubt myself, thought I was crazy and losing my mind. My emotions and feelings were always on overdrive, giving me anxiety. Making me unhinged, but that dark doubtful past is behind me. 
my husband tells me, when he talks about a person..."I hope youre not trying to feel him/her". I get angry becuz I don't control it... Sometimes spirits just pop up & talks, you cant run anywhere because they follow you.
Trust me, if I can control them...I would have my business hours posted so the spirits dont disturb me at random times in the night. 
This is why my ultimate fantasy is to be stuck on a deserted island with NO ONE. 
Its called sensory overload. Yes its a thing

posts.caption:
A man approached me asking to learn about mugyo, the sacred traditions of our ancestors. Being a diaspora, wasnt exposed to the culture, etiquette and traditions of Korea. 
He immediately asked for my birthday, and I declined. I explained that you dont ask a mudang for personal information. Its not proper nor seen as respectful. 
I invited him to a FB group, hoping he can share his own experiences with others like him and learn about mugyo as well. His tone wasnt respectful or cordial, instead the man-child got upset because I explained he was disrespectful. 
Your earth age has no relevancy when speaking with a mudang. Traditionally even my parents need to speak to me using honorifics. 
When a person becomes a monk, they throw away their old "self" becomes anew. Even their parents cannot treat the monk as their child, and speak to the monk like they use to. They must use honorifics when speaking to their monk child. Even in korean history, the royalty addressed a mudang with respect.
If I took him on as apprentice, initiated him as mudang, he would need to call me, mom. Doesnt matter that hes 7 yrs older than me. His lack of understanding of my culture showed and he threw a temper tantrum equivalent to my 4 year old. 
He said to me, that I should bow down to him...he shouldn't bow down to me. That hes old enough to be my father. 
What a twisted psychotic fool.
I guess he also isnt aware that you never disrespect a mudang with their gods/deities because it will come back to him. 
His ignorance was astounding, his arrogance reeked with Western entitlement. 
#ignoranceatitsfinest #mudang #shaman #koreanshaman #mugyo #entitlement

Happy Chuseok #추석 its the Korean Harvest Festival. Offerings are all up, including the traditional dishes like #토란국 taro soup and #송펀 half moon rice cakes. 
Traditionally, this holiday you visit family from your hometown, visit ancestral graves and hold memorial called charye to honor your ancestors. A beautiful day to give thanks and gratitude. 
Preparing for todays offerings took 3 days including today, all the dishes were handmade and prepared by me. Its not easy since I am due in 2 weeks with a baby, but still its my duty as a caretaker to my gods and ancestral deities. 
Have a beautiful Chuseok everyone.

posts.caption:
Had a dream yesterday, Owkhwangsangje (옥황상제) known as the Jade Emperor of Heaven appeared. Behind him the sky was beautifully clear and the grass beneath him was a verdant green. The heavenly blue sky had multiple stars shining or sun's blazing, and the Jade Emperor 옥황상제, said to me, "this is the land of the stars 별나라". Then he pointed to the star next to me and said, "this star right here, is the brightest one in the sky. The star fate destiny of a high Buddhist monk" 
That was it for my dream, as I woke immediately after. The first thought that popped into my head was that 옥황상제 Jade Emperor was talking about my child. Even my spirit mother told me that's how she interpreted that dream. 
옥황상제 is known as the Jade Emperor of Heaven or Hwanin the Divine Regent is the highest being in mugyo. In the Korean mythology, the son of Hwanin/Jade Emperor is Dangun, he is the initiator of all mudang shamans and our ancestor. The mudang shaman lineage is thought to be part of heavenly royalty, descendants of the Heavenly King

posts.caption:
There is a saying amongst Korean mudang shaman (무당) and Buddhist monks (스님) that when a child had their umbilical cord wrapped around his/her neck. Their fate destiny saju (사주) is to become either a 무당 (mudang) and/or 스님 (monk). When my spirit mom was born, with her umbilical cord around her neck. A high level monk asked her mom to give away the baby so that she can train to become a high level monk at a temple in the mountain. 
The umbilical cord wrapped around the neck is a sign of predestined fate to walk a path of higher consciousness, and serve the gods/deities. 
My spirit mom said made sense since I am a mudang shaman, and this baby being gifted from the gods. That this child shall walk a similar path to mine. I always knew that this child will be called, as my dream foretold when he was conceived. At a time when doctors told me I couldn't have anymore kids, my gods came to me in a dream gifting me gifts of pearls. Went to the doctor office the very next day to confirm. Its bittersweet for me, as I know very well what this path requires.

posts.caption:
Another early morning waking. 
Can't figure out why....as too many factors come into play. 
Is it because of the initiation kut at the end of the month, is it my gods and ancestral deities waking me up for prayer/meditation, or insomnia issue because I'm in my 3rd trimester of my pregnancy? 
Figured since I cant sleep, peek my head in for my morning greetings, prayer and meditation to my gods and deities. 
Prayers have been somewhat lacking as the pregnancy makes me more lethargic, I ask for mercy and give my gratitude. Recite a few Buddhist sutras, as I have not fully learned the chuksa 축사 prayer of a mudang. Plus I dont think my family and neighbors would appreciate the drums and gong banging in the wee hours of the morning on a Sunday. 
My life is different, and my duties and dedication as a caretaker to my shrine/temple comes first (also my family). Its so hard to time away from my temple. I dont go on trips or vacays, its hard to free up time to chat with friends or meet for coffee. I dont have much hobbies other than meditation, prayer work or mudang shaman work. I keep my schedule open for my clients, as they can show up randomly without appointments. Or I just spend my day with my mudang spirit mother, as our relationship/bond is more than teacher and apprentice. I feel so honored and blessed to have such a person like her by my side to guide me. Truly. This life is just a blessing. 
Have a beautiful Sunday 🤗💗 #earlymorningrisings #koreanshaman #koreanshamanism #shaman #shamanism #shamaniccall #gods #deities #shrine #temple #sacredspace #altar #gratitude

posts.caption:
How do you define a calling? Why is that ppl question my path/judgement, is it because its not the norm. Would you question a person who felt the calling to submit their life to God by becoming a priest? Or question someone who wants to shave their head, and become a Buddhist monk? 
The process of becoming a priest is institutionalized. Going to theology priest school, obtaining a degree and finally getting their certification, passing their exam...like a lawyer or doctor. That process does not certify their ability to become a priest, validate their spiritual calling or guarantee their life path be straight.
Someone asked me if I was certified. I didnt know whether to laugh or get angry. Like as if an institution can verify if I am a shaman mudang or not, sounds ridiculous to me. Its not a list of credits I need, or series of written test I need to pass. 
Shamanism existed long before ANY religion ever came to. Its found all over the world practiced by the earliest civilizations. Its not an imported belief like Christianity or Catholicism. Pls dont think I am attacking other beliefs, just asking for open mindedness. 
In my culture, to be a recognized mudang shaman priestess is to be verified by the spirits. No man or woman can be the judge of that except for the spirits and your mudang teacher.  It involves the initiation ceremony to become a shaman
Nowadays calling oneself a shaman is just a mere advertising marketing strategy. It offends me that many use the term without ever really knowing what it really means to be one. Its more than connecting or communicating with spirits....its actually having one foot in this physical world and the other in the spirit world, walking it simultaneously. Working for the benefits of the spirits moreso than man. 
Pls be respectful, I am proud to be called one, honored that the gods has chosen me to be their intermediary.

posts.caption:
Picture from Google. Not my drawing

It took me a really long time to realize what I was experiencing. There was no one that I can talk to or even ask questions. I had no guidance and left alone to figure out things. 
Awakening or Enlightenment is such a destructive process, its a sacred destruction. For me, happened a few times mixed with the calling of the spirits. It was hell on Earth, not a casual conversation you can talk about with your bestie. 
Before accepting this path, the few people I would open up to about this probably looked at me like I was a crazy person. Rambling on and talking about the fear of being marked, chosen and seeing things unexplainable. 
The more you fight it, the worse it gets. The lack of sleep because of the shadows, the fear of the dark, the vivid dreams, the sleep paralysis and straight up seeing spirits....messes and f$%# with your head and mental stability. 
It was such a hard and difficult time for me, I wanted to run away but then I had a child (my son) which I dreamt about...my grandmother who passed yrs ago came back to tell me in a dream, I was expecting.
My health was at its worse, surgery after surgery...bad luck after bad luck, everything was going wrong. Everything was so messed up, felt like the rain was beating me down every single day. 
Until I finally told my mom, about the the little girl who would visit me when ever I had a sleep paralysis attack.... Mom had an older sister that contracted the measles and passed just shy of 5 years old. 
My mom confessed to me recently, that she knew what was happening to me. She said I was always different as a child, talking about dead people and the gods of my culture. She thought sending me to Church was going to cure me. 
My Catholic paternal family wanted to reach out to priest to for an exorcism. Till my Uncle realized too that nothing will work, this calling was far more ancient and older, stronger than Christianity or Catholicism.

Had a kut 굿 ceremony yesterday. 
It wasnt the client's first 굿, she had one last winter. She said in the beginning she didnt fully believe in our tradition, didnt have faith in the gods and deities. Only to realize during the kut ceremony, it was one of her ancestral spirits that had passed on at a young age from drowning in the water. We call that ji-ki 지기, or I guess the English is term is empathy.  When you make contact with a spirit, and they pass on all their feelings, messages, bodily aches and pains.

posts.caption:
I was explaining and speaking about the intensive training of a "newly born" mudang manshin shaman. 
Best way to explain the intensive training is... that the art of a mudang, is similar to a giaseng or courtesean. We must learn the arts of dancing, singing, the multiple musical instruments, learning the poetry and calligraphy of hanja, proper etiquette and so much more. 
While giaseng and courtesean, entertained men and their guests. We, mudangs are the entertainers of the gods and the spirits. Our path is never-ending, and always something new to learn. We must carry ourselves with pose and learn how to soften our hearts with compassion. Even when our patience and limits are pushed to the edge...us, mudang shaman must always try to act in a composed manner despite the many people who may spit in our faces. 
We are beings walking a higher conscious path, and our actions and intentions must reflect that. Always aware, always conscious. Let karma, nature and our gods protect us from those who wrong us. I do not worry because I know my gods will react accordingly .

posts.caption:
What is a Mudang ?
The word "mu" is ancient word describing a shaman-priest intermediary between the first god, gods of nature and humans in the korean indigenous religion. 
The men shaman priest are usually called bak-su, and mudangs are referred to women. The baksu word is an adaptation of Siberian names for male shamans baksi, balsi, bahsih, etc. 
Mudang is a priestess who employs magic to effect cures, tell fortune, soothe the spirits of the dead, repulse evils, and so forth. Mudang (mostly) has hereditary abilities to contact the spirit world, inhabited by various shamanic gods and deities. 
No person chooses the path of a mudang voluntarily, even if its hereditary. The path of a mudang involves alot of grief and loneliness, misunderstanding and ridicule. Only the true mudangs are chosen by the spirits experiencing sinbyeong known as the divine sickness, shamanic sickness, spirit sickness, etc.

posts.caption:
The 무가 (muga), songs of a Korean shaman. 
Nothing within the Korean shaman culture is written down in terms of manuscripts or instruction. Knowledge of the korean shamanic culture is usually and normally passed down orally from shaman to their apprentice. 
I purchased this hoping to gain better insight.
The songs of a shaman, is performed during a kut ceremony when the spirits of ancestors, gods and deities are invoked. 
Each shaman songs varies, by the shaman style. The lyrics to the song isnt set and changes. But this book wasnt too helpful because it was written and interpreted by an outsider, an observerer of the Korean shaman culture.

"From prehistory to the era of the Three Kingdom, it is thought that Koreans did not believe in Heaven or Hell, but in the Next Life that existed outside of time and place"
Sometime in the 4th or 5th century with the introduction of Buddhism, where it adopted traditional indigenous practices including Heaven, Hell, different levels of Hell and the afterlife. 
Unlike other shamanic culture, the Korean indigenous shaman culture intertwines with Buddhism along with Korean folklore and mythology. In our shaman world of gods and deities, all are equally respected in their field.
I feel incredibly honored and blessed to partake in the ancient traditional culture of my ancestors. I hope that this ancient culture and tradition is something I can help pass down.

posts.caption:
Korean shamanism. 
What is shinbyeong, known as the shaman sickness or divine sickness. 
It hard to say what is and what isnt, as every shaman experiences different types of shinbyeong. No two shamans experience the same sickness or illness, and having shinbyeong isnt a set of symotons that you can mark off a checklist. 
Shinbyeong comes in a form that has no medical reason or treatment. Its also a series of horrid bad luck as the spirits interfere with your daily life. Its a very destructive process that peels away at you everyday for years. 
At first the signs are subtle, nothing seems out of the ordinary but quickly things will spiral down fast. The only way to stop this is to have a mudang/manshin have a ceremony to help you accept the destined path or make the spirits sleep.
I had to have a kut ceremony so I can transform, a rebirth to accept the calling of the gods and my ancestral spirits who came back as deities. Born with the star fate destiny of a mudang shaman, I had no other option than to accept this path and fate. The gods were angry that I did not acknowledge this path sooner, but nevertheless happy that I finally found my way home. My mother was suppose to be a shaman but never accepted this fate so when I was born it was determined by heaven and the gods that I will walk this journey in her stead.

posts.caption:
Love the interior of the old weathered temple. I find more beauty in this, than the newly built temples. The old beams tells many stories of how many storms its has endured, the floors creeks while singing to us about the many people they have supported. I love old things, love the history, the scars and the journey it tells. 
Looking back at my own childhood, it was very different than my friends growing up. While everyone played outside on the weekends, watching cartoons. I was out in prayer with my family at an outdoor catholic shrine past midnight regardless of the weather, rain or snow. 
In elementary Catholic school every one thought I was the weird girl, meanwhile I was just trying to fing a place where I belonged, trying hard to fit in. Since I was young...i've seen and sense things that normal people couldnt. I would lay awake at night terrified of the dark and the secrets the corners of my room had. 
No one can understand that, and so I always walked and lived my life dancing on the edge of what should be. 
I don't care if people doesnt understand me, or believe me. All my life experiences has brought me to this point in my life. I feel more alive now since I have accepted all the parts of me....including my other world of spirits. Its not for everyone, or for you....its for me. This spirited world I now gracefully dance is a path for me, part of my soul path, while yours may be to live a life part of society norms. Mine is to dance on the edge of it, and I have never been more free and whole.

posts.caption:
I was walking along a nature preserve, and came across an old family burial cemetery. And it made me think about our relationship with our ancestors. In my traditional culture, the relationship with your ancestors is very important. As our time moves into modernism, those traditions of ancestral respect gets left behind. 
I had a man in his late 40s come to home for a reading.  He had a lot of stress and worries, I was able to tell that he had restless sleep, with vivid dreams and constant wakings. I was flustered at first because I wasnt sure what to say to him. But as soon as we enteres my temple, thats when I got hit with all sorts of emotions and images. I just started talking about his past, and told him he was very successful with his business up until 5 years ago. 5 years ago is when all his troubles started, and he told me that it was right. 
For this man, sensed that most of his troubles stemmed from his ancestors. He needed a kut, to help relieve the anguish of his ancestors and with their help give him lots of luck and fortune. I felt bad, telling someone that...felt sad for thr bad because I can tell he was a genuine good hearted person. I really wished I can help him more, told him to pray and have a small ceremony for his ancestors to pay his respect.

posts.caption:
My husband's friend came by to see us, we went out for dinner and drinks. As we were heading up the front porch stairs, he asked me if I can do a reading for him. 
I felt my throat tighten up and get all knotted inside. Part of me didn't want to do a reading, as I was in a bright cheerful mood. But truthfully and honestly, I didnt have much faith and belief that I might be able to connect with him. I didnt believe in myself and the gifts I was given.
But as soon as he said those words, and asked me for a reading. Thats when I started to get my feelings, my body felt heavier and I began to see images. Before we got to front door..i began sensing his emotions and his experiences. 
We spoke for a long while and immediately spirits came through.  I told him about the different people around him, about who I sensed and see. I told him things that he has never said to anyone before, told him about his family background that I couldn't possibly know. 
At one point I felt his energy soften and he began to open up, I felt all his emotions and described some ailments he has. He shook his head in disbelief, he told me how scary it was how I knew things. My body would take on the things that bothers him, the labored breathing, heart palpitations, heavy shoulder, weak knees. In my culture we call that tigi, when your body takes on their aliments. 
Either way, I thanked him for the opportunity to read him, to allow me to connect and giving me the assurance that I shouldnt doubt myself. I was grateful.... once again I am shown that I can really connect, and should believe more, have more faith

Happy Lunar New Year (설날) everyone 😚😍
It is one of the most significant traditional Korean holidays, celebration usually lasting 3 days. Its also a day when family gathers and perform ancestral ceremony call charye. 
Today is a special day when we prepare tteokguk (떡국), as it was in ancient times. The white tteok rice cake symbolizes purity and cleanliness, ritually eaten for New Year good fortune. 
I poured my heart into todays LNY offerings. I hope my gods, deities and ancestors know how grateful I am, and hopefully help me more in the New Year. 
Have a beautiful blessed New Year everyone.

posts.caption:
Becoming a shaman - pt 2
Only 2 ways of becoming a shaman, and that is being marked and chosen by the Spirits directly. Second way is through your ancestral blood lineage, meaning that someone from your family was a shaman. The spirits will pass down through the blood lineage, usually skipping every other generation...but some cases it doesnt, like me. 
I asked before following this path and accepting this fate, if my children are spared from this. The answer was no, my child will bear the same burden as I because the spirits that I have are too strong. The gods, the spirits came from both my paternal and maternal side of my family. 
Please dont be confused, there is nothing wrong with learning some of the skills and techniques we use to benefit your personal life. In korea, some people would perform a simple house cleansing that they learned from their neighborhood shaman. But that doesnt qualify them to be a shaman chasing away negativity from a home. 
The problem I have with, are the people who hasn't the slightest clue as to what a true shaman is. Not denying or doubting your spirituality or your spiritual path, but please refrain from calling yourself a shaman. That special honor is reserved for those who the Spirits has marked and chosen.
*on a side note, the pic is a shrine dedicated to the dragon god. We put our offerings, and pray.
